Title: Dollar holds losses as markets await Fed minutes, speakers
Article:
TOKYO: The US dollar remained lower on Wednesday after stress in European bond markets abated and as eyes turned to the release of Federal Reserve minutes and speeches by its policymakers for signals on a potential rate hike.
The euro surged by the most in seven weeks in the prior session as French bond yields slid after the frontrunner in next spring's presidential election outlined plans to slash spending. The yen weakened even after a dovish Bank of Japan board member said she would support interest rate increases.
Later on Wednesday, the US central bank is due to release minutes of its September 15-16 policy meeting when it raised interest rates to contend with inflation. Comments from Fed policymakers have come across as less hawkish following lower-than-expected personal consumption expenditures (PCE) data and jobs data last week.
"There seems to be a little bit less urgency on the Fed to hike rates after the softer PCE and then the nonfarm payroll reports recently," Gavin Friend, a senior markets strategist at National Australia Bank, said on a podcast.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose 0.03 per cent to 101.94, following a 0.27 per cent slide in the prior session. The euro eased 0.08 per cent to US$1.1249.
The Japanese yen weakened 0.19 per cent against the greenback to 158.43 per dollar. Sterling dipped 0.08 per cent to US$1.3262.
Bond yields around the world have climbed in recent weeks due to expectations of central bank rate hikes as well as concerns about government finances.
French debt is under growing pressure as politicians struggle to curb the budget deficit ahead of a divisive election in 2027. The calling of a snap election in Spain added to the recent stress on the euro.
The euro rallied sharply on Tuesday after far-right French presidential candidate Marine Le Pen raised her target for spending cuts to €140 billion (US$158 billion) from €125 billion in savings originally planned if she wins power in 2027.
The Bank of Japan's new policymaker Ayano Sato said in an interview with the Kyodo news agency on Wednesday that she supports the idea of raising interest rates in several stages.
The BOJ may signal this month that underlying inflation has roughly hit its 2 per cent target, three people familiar with its thinking said, highlighting its readiness to raise interest rates again.
OCTOBER FED HIKE EXPECTATIONS RETREAT
Expectations for a Fed rate hike later this month have retreated but markets are still anticipating more increases later in the year and next year.
In contrast to the recent call for patience from some Fed officials, Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said on Tuesday that the central bank still needs to raise its policy rate further to lower inflation, even if higher long-term yields are weighing on activity in some parts of the economy.
The chance of a hike of at least 25 basis points in October stands at 20.5 per cent, from about 51 per cent a week ago, according to CME FedWatch, but markets are pricing in an 84.5 per cent chance of a hike at the December meeting.
"With little forward guidance from Chair (Kevin) Warsh, markets have reacted sharply to each US data release and policymaker speech," Commonwealth Bank of Australia currency strategist Samara Hammoud said in a report. "We expect the Fed to wait until December before hiking again."
Fed officials Christopher Waller, Neel Kashkari and Alberto Musalem are all due to speak later on Wednesday. The central bank is also scheduled to release consumer credit data, which is expected to show a decrease to US$15 billion in August from US$18.06 billion in July.
The Australian dollar weakened 0.04 per cent versus the greenback to US$0.6979, while the kiwi slid 0.07 per cent to US$0.5617.
In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 0.22 per cent to US$85,438.59, and ether declined 0.12 per cent to US$2,695.22.

Title: House arrest rules still being finalised, says Saifuddin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rules on the use of closed-circuit television (CCTV), electronic ankle tags and permitted visitors for house arrest are still being finalised, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said.
He said there were currently no house arrest orders issued under a specific law as the proposed legislation was still being finalised and undergoing legal review by the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC).
"The government has, in principle, agreed to establish a legal framework to allow remand detainees who meet certain conditions to be considered for house arrest.
"This would be an alternative to placement in prison while they await trial," he said in a parliamentary written reply.
He said the relevant aspects would be subject to provisions under the law, regulations and standard operating procedures that were still being finalised.
Saifuddin was responding to Lim Lip Eng (PH-Kepong), who asked about the number of house arrest orders issued.
Lim also asked whether people under house arrest would be required to undergo CCTV monitoring, wear electronic monitoring devices and what categories of visitors would be allowed.
On Sept 18, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, granted former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional house arrest.
This allowed him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to him paying the RM50 million fine imposed over his conviction in the SRC International case.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin clarified that a conditional pardon granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong was different from a house arrest order proposed under the House Arrest Bill.
"Conditional pardon is a prerogative of pardon under the Federal Constitution, and its implementation is subject to the decisions and conditions set by the relevant pardoning authority," he said.
Therefore, he said, a person placed under home confinement following a conditional pardon could not be directly equated with a house arrest order issued by a court under a specific Act.
For conditional pardons, Saifuddin said any conditions relating to control, movement monitoring, visits or other matters would be subject to the decisions and conditions set by the relevant authority.
He said the applicable implementation procedures would also apply.
"For example, where a prisoner is required to remain at a residence under a conditional pardon, matters such as visits, control and movement monitoring would need to be detailed through the relevant standard operating procedures," he said.

Title: Form Two student's death: Investigation papers referred to A-GC today
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Police will refer the investigation papers into the death of a 14-year-old male student at a school in the district to the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) today.
District police chief Superintendent Muhamad Mustafah Hussin said no decision had been made so far on whether to charge any suspect in court, and police were awaiting further instructions after the investigation papers were referred to the A-GC.
"As of now, no decision has been made on the date to charge the suspect in the case, which is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code following an incident at a school in Kuala Pilah last month," he said when contacted today.
Muhammad Idlan Fareeq Shahril was reported to have been found unconscious at about 8pm on Sept 25 at the hostel of a sports school in Kuala Pilah.
The victim was taken to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital (HTAN), where he was pronounced dead.
Following the incident, two 16-year-old male teenagers, who were seniors of the victim, were detained
to assist in the investigation
, with police classifying the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
The remand of the first suspect had been extended until tomorrow, while the second suspect's remand had been extended until Friday.

Title: Ringgit opens marginally lower against US dollar amid mixed global cues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened marginally lower against the US dollar on Wednesday, with the local note still trading within a narrow trading range amid mixed global market cues.
At 8 am, the ringgit eased slightly to 4.0840/0885 against the US dollar from Tuesday's close of 4.0835/0880.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the 0.33 per cent decline in the US Dollar Index (DXY) to 101.833 points, together with Brent crude prices hovering around US$100 per barrel, provided some support for the ringgit.
He said global equities were also positive on optimism over corporate earnings, reflecting stronger sentiment in financial markets "On that note, improved risk appetite among traders is providing support to the ringgit today," he told Bernama.
The ringgit also traded mostly lower against major currencies at the opening.
It fell against the British pound to 5.4174/4234 from 5.4066/4125 at Tuesday's close and dipped against the euro to 4.5949/6000 from 4.5907/5957. However, it strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.5794/5824 from 2.5807/5837.
The ringgit also traded mostly lower against regional currencies.
It dipped against the Thai baht to 12.1439/1627 from 12.1424/1609 and against the Singapore dollar to 3.1956/1994 from 3.1935/1975 at Tuesday's close.
The local note was unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.50/6.51 and was almost flat against the Indonesian rupiah at 228.1/228.5.

Title: 11 measures proposed to strengthen healthcare workforce in Sabah, Sarawak
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Eleven immediate measures have been proposed to strengthen the healthcare workforce in Sabah and Sarawak, including better incentives, career pathways and family support.
Senator Dr R. A. Lingeshwaran said the proposals were aimed at making postings in the two states fairer, more attractive and sustainable for healthcare professionals.
The proposed measures include a clear 24-month standard service period.
Doctors with satisfactory performance could then apply for transfers, specialist training or their next placement.
Lingeshwaran also called for priority pathways to specialist training for doctors who complete their required service in Sabah and Sarawak while meeting prescribed key performance indicators.
Other proposals include restoring the Regional Incentive Payment (Bayaran Insentif Wilayah) based on a percentage of salary instead of a fixed rate.
A rural and remote posting hardship allowance of at least RM1,000 a month was also proposed.
The package also calls for suitable accommodation for officers before they report for duty.
Government quarters or housing allowances should reflect actual rental rates where quarters are unavailable, he said.
The Health Ministry should provide advance payments for approved relocation expenses, including air tickets, excess baggage and transportation.
This would prevent newly posted doctors from having to bear thousands of ringgit in upfront costs, he said.
For officers serving a 24-month term, the government should also consider periodic return airfares to Peninsular Malaysia, such as once every six months, subject to established terms and conditions.
Lingeshwaran said service in Sabah and Sarawak, particularly in rural and remote areas, should receive additional recognition in specialist training applications, scholarships, promotions and subsequent placement preferences.
He also proposed a retention incentive for doctors who continue serving beyond the initial 24-month period.
However, he stressed that financial incentives alone would not resolve workforce shortages.
The Health Ministry would also need to ensure reasonable doctor-patient ratios, manageable on-call duties, access to annual leave and adequate replacement staff.
Family support should include assistance with school placement, healthcare access, transportation, accommodation and other essential living facilities.
The proposals should also extend beyond doctors to nurses, pharmacists, dental officers, allied health professionals and other critical healthcare personnel, he added.
"The shortage of doctors cannot be addressed in isolation. The entire healthcare team must be adequately staffed," he said in a statement made available to Media Prima.
Lingeshwaran said the government could also introduce an interim package within three months.
It would cover the 24-month service period, salary-based Regional Incentive Payment (BIW), RM1,000 rural hardship allowance, proper accommodation, relocation costs, return airfares and a clear career pathway.
"This approach is not simply about compelling doctors to report for duty.
"It is about making service in Sabah and Sarawak fairer, more attractive and sustainable for healthcare professionals," he added.
The Parliamentary Special Select Committee on Health wants the Health Ministry to review existing allowances and incentives to encourage medical officers to serve in Sabah and Sarawak.
Special Select Committee on Health member Young Syefura Othman said the refusal of medical officers to take up postings in the two states was a serious concern.
She said some
hospitals
were operating with as few as three medical officers.

Title: Oil prices rise as storms and air strikes threaten supply
Article:
PERTH: Oil prices rose on Wednesday as the market weighed supply constraints from a storm heading for US oil-producing regions and attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia against increased supplies of Middle East crude.
Brent futures rose 93 cents, or 0.92 per cent, to US$101.51 a barrel by 0022 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 82 cents, or 0.92 per cent, to US$90.25.
US forecasters said on Tuesday a storm forming in the Gulf of Mexico would become the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 within two days and would likely hit oil and gas producing facilities.
The offshore areas in the Gulf in the storm's path produce 15 per cent of US crude oil and 5 per cent of the country's natural gas.
KCM Trade chief analyst Tim Waterer said the storm was an "unwelcome complication for crude, raising the prospect of production and refining disruptions at a time when the market already has enough supply-side headaches".
The storm could affect six refineries.
Refineries in US Gulf states account for about 50 per cent of the national capacity of 18.2 million barrels per day (bpd).
US crude oil and gasoline inventories fell, while distillate stocks rose marginally last week, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.
Crude stocks fell by 2.09 million barrels in the week ended Oct 2.
Supply had been rising as the East-West pipeline hit 5.8 million barrels a day, according to Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman on Tuesday.
Around 12 million barrels per day of crude oil and 2 million bpd of refined products were leaving the Middle East on tankers in the last 7 to 10 days, the head of Vitol said.
However, Saudi Arabia's airports in Jazan and Najran were targeted in two attacks on Monday evening, the Saudi aviation authority said, as hostilities between the kingdom and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis escalated.
The attacks occurred as Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces pressed a major offensive to retake territory from the Houthis, after weeks of rebel advances, with Riyadh stepping up airstrikes in support of the campaign.
Attacks and refinery outages are "likely to keep the cracks elevated and scarcity will transmit to crude. Prices will stay elevated near a US$100 level without any material de-escalation emerging," said Mukesh Sahdev, chief oil analyst at X Analysts in Sydney.
US-Iran relations are no closer to repair with US President Donald Trump saying on Tuesday that nobody knew who was running Iran during the eight-month US-Israeli war with Iran.
"Their leaders are gone, their second group of leaders are gone, and the biggest problem I have is nobody knows who the hell is running the country," Trump said.
Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said on Sunday Washington knows very well who their counterpart is in Iran and how the decision-making system in Iran works.

Title: Porsche extends aftersales reach to Sarawak
Article:
PORSCHE Malaysia has expanded its aftersales network to Sarawak and Sabah with the opening of Porsche Service Centre Kuching, its first authorised Porsche service facility in the region.
The facility, operated in partnership with Hap Seng Prestige, provides Porsche owners in Sarawak with access to authorised maintenance, diagnostics and repair services without having to send their vehicles to Peninsular Malaysia.
Porsche Malaysia, represented by Sime Darby Auto Performance Sdn Bhd, said the new centre would bring Porsche-certified aftersales support closer to customers in the state.
The 1S service centre has a two-bay workshop staffed by Porsche-trained technicians and equipped with specialised diagnostic systems and workshop equipment.
It also has a customer lounge, while Genuine Porsche Parts are sourced through Porsche's global supply network for servicing and repairs.
The appointment of Hap Seng Prestige builds on Hap Seng Group's automotive retail and aftersales experience, with the partnership aimed at providing Porsche owners in Sarawak with authorised technical support.
The centre's opening comes as Porsche Malaysia expands its presence beyond its existing network in Peninsular Malaysia, giving owners in east Malaysia more direct access to the marque's aftersales infrastructure.
Porsche Malaysia said the service centre would support routine maintenance as well as diagnostics and repairs, with vehicles serviced according to Porsche's global standards.
To mark the opening, Porsche owners in Sarawak are being invited to a service clinic featuring a complimentary 111-point inspection of their vehicles.
The inspection covers the overall condition of the vehicle and is intended to identify maintenance or service requirements.
Customers can also take up Porsche approved warranty packages available during the Service Clinic.
The new facility will also carry a selection of Porsche Tequipment accessories and Porsche Lifestyle merchandise.
The expansion gives Porsche owners in Sarawak a dedicated local point for authorised aftersales support, while strengthening the brand's service coverage across Malaysia.

Title: 17-year-old girl reported missing in Tanah Merah
Article:
TANAH MERAH: Police are seeking the public's help to locate a 17-year-old girl who has been reported missing since Saturday.
Tanah Merah district police chief, Superintendent Mohd Haki Hasbullah, said the girl was identified as Nur Aleeya Natasha Mohd Sabri, 17.
He said her family lodged a police report about her disappearance at 5pm yesterday.
"She was believed to have left home at midnight on Saturday before she could no longer be contacted.
"She is about 157cm tall and weighs 47kg. Her last known address is Jalan Klinik here," he said.
Mohd Haki wants anyone with information to contact investigating officer Sergeant Mohamad Airel Ashraf Rosli at 010-5670798.
They can also contact the Tanah Merah district police headquarters hotline at 09-9558429 or 09-9556222, the Kelantan contingent police headquarters hotline at 09-7455622 or any nearby police station.

Title: BYD draws 800 owners for football legends event
Article:
MORE than 800 BYD owners, staff, partners and management gathered in Kuala Lumpur for a two-day event featuring a line-up of former football stars.
Organised by BYD Sime Motors, the AllStar Legends experience brought together former Premier League and international players including Steven Gerrard, Michael Owen, Ryan Giggs, Alessandro Del Piero, Dida and Javier Saviola.
The event, held on Oct 2 and 3, included meet-and-greet sessions, a Legends Talk, gala dinner and an AllStar Legends football match at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre.
The football legends also toured Kuala Lumpur and made appearances at BYD Glenmarie and BYD TREC Kuala Lumpur, travelling in BYD vehicles.
For participating families, one of the highlights was the selection of children from BYD-owning families as player mascots.
The children walked onto the pitch alongside the football legends before the match.
BYD Malaysia managing director Jacob Ma said the event reflected the company's "Build Your Dreams" philosophy, which he said was about encouraging people to pursue their ambitions.
"The legends we welcomed to Malaysia changed the game through talent, dedication and an unwavering pursuit of excellence," he said.
Sime Motors Southeast Asia managing director Jeffrey Gan said the event was intended to strengthen ties between BYD and its growing owner community.
"Ownership extends far beyond the vehicle itself. As our community continues to grow, we remain committed to creating memorable experiences that strengthen our connection with our owners," he said.
The event also provided an opportunity for BYD owners to meet fellow drivers and take part in activities beyond their usual ownership experience.
BYD Seal owner Sam Khoo said meeting the football legends and attending the gala dinner and match was a memorable experience.
For parents of the selected Kid Mascots, the occasion offered a chance for their children to be involved in the event alongside international football stars.
Fatin, a BYD Sealion 7 owner, said seeing her child walk onto the pitch with the football legends was a proud moment for the family.

Title: When it's about safety, be proactive not reactive
Article:
LETTERS: The tragic death of a 16-year-old schoolgirl in Negri Sembilan is not just one sad event. Similar incidents have happened before.
It is a warning we have ignored for too long the need to be proactive rather than reactive in anything we do.
Time and again, we see the same pattern: a disaster happens, we speak about it when we react and then we do nothing — until the next tragedy.
This is not leadership. This is waiting for harm before we act. We have seen this with our own eyes.
Structures along our highways have collapsed. Roads have failed. Reports have pointed out risks.
Yet our authorities almost always act only after something goes wrong rather than taking proactive action to prevent an accident.
We say "better safe than sorry" — but too often, we choose sorry. Safety cannot start when an accident happens. It must start long before.
What we need is a real culture of prevention and acting before a tragedy. That means fixing problems when they are small — not waiting until they become big and dangerous.
It means checking our roads, bridges, and public facilities regularly. It means proper and regular maintenance, scheduled checks, and quick repairs.
We should not wait for a road to fall apart before we fix it. This is most important in our schools. Every child deserves to be safe while they learn. That means constant watch over school grounds, buildings, and all activities.
It means putting clear measures in place to stop violence before it starts. We must not wait for another incident to tighten rules, improve supervision, or make our schools secure.
Prevention is not extra work — it is our duty. It costs far less to keep things safe than to fix what breaks. More than that: it saves lives.
We owe it to our children, our families, and our country to change the way we think.
Let us stop acting only after tragedy strikes. Let us look ahead, plan ahead, and protect ahead. A safer Malaysia is built not when we grieve — but when we decide to prevent.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
Kuala Lumpur
The views expressed in this article are the author's own and do not necessarily reflect those of the New Straits Times

Title: Police continue probe into Jempol MP's alleged campaign remarks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are still investigating Jempol member of parliament Datuk Shamsulkahar Deli over remarks he allegedly made while campaigning during the Negri Sembilan election.
The investigation papers were returned by the state prosecution office for further action, the Home Ministry said.
The ministry said the initial stage of the investigation had been completed before the papers were referred to the Negri Sembilan prosecution office on Aug 21 for review and further instructions.
"On Sept 3, the investigation papers were returned to the police with several further instructions for the investigating officer to act on.
"Investigations are still ongoing to complete the matters as instructed, and the investigation papers will be resubmitted to the Negri Sembilan prosecution office for further instructions," it said in a written parliamentary reply yesterday.
The ministry was responding to R. S. N. Rayer (PH-Jelutong), who asked why Shamsulkahar had yet to be charged in court for any criminal offence despite allegedly making defamatory and inflammatory remarks while campaigning during the state election.
The investigation papers were opened under the Penal Code, Election Offences Act 1954 and Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
The investigation followed allegations that Shamsulkahar had made defamatory remarks linking a political party to a caricature deemed insulting to the Selangor Sultan while campaigning during the state election.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said 62 police reports were received between July 18 and July 28.
He said 19 investigation papers relating to election offences were opened.

Title: Polisas to cooperate in probe into student allegedly strangled to death
Article:
KUANTAN: The Polytechnic and Community College Education Department will give its cooperation to police investigating the death of a student at Jalan Air Putih yesterday.
Expressing its condolences over the incident, the department said M. Elisa Jonova, 19, a diploma student at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Polytechnic (Polisas), was found unconscious yesterday.
"The case is currently under investigation by the authorities. The department and Polisas will give full cooperation to assist in the investigation and leave it to the authorities to conduct a thorough probe.
"We urge all quarters not to speculate or disseminate unverified information and to respect the privacy of the deceased's family during this difficult time," it said in a statement.
The statement said the department and Polisas would continue to provide the necessary support and assistance to the deceased's family.
Yesterday, it was reported that a female student was found dead at about 4.30am, believed to have been
strangled
following an argument with her boyfriend, inside a house.
The 19-year-old suspect, who contacted police after the incident, has been remanded until Oct 12 to assist in the murder investigation.
Meanwhile, Polisas expressed its sorrow and condolences to the victim's family in a Facebook post, which also included a photograph of the victim.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zara Qairina's mother arrives at court to testify
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The late Zara Qairina Mahathir's mother, Noraidah Lamat, arrived at the Kota Kinabalu Court Complex this morning to testify at the inquest into her daughter's death.
Dressed in a baju kurung and wearing a face mask, Noraidah arrived carrying a JusticeForZara poster.
She appeared calm as she entered the court complex, accompanied by her legal team.
Proceedings are being conducted before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan.
As of yesterday, 81 witnesses had testified since the inquest began on Sept 3, 2025.
Zara was found unconscious on the ground floor of her school hostel on July 16, 2025.
She was pronounced dead the following day at Queen Elizabeth Hospital.
Her remains were exhumed on Aug 9, 2025, before a post-mortem examination was conducted the following day at the Forensic Medicine Department of Queen Elizabeth Hospital.
On Aug 20, 2025, five minors, identified by the pseudonyms Students A, B, C, D and E, were charged in the Court for Childresn with insulting Zara.
All five pleaded not guilty and the trial is ongoing.

Title: [UPDATED] Emotion, tears as Messi retires from Argentina national team
Article:
BUENOS AIRES: Lionel Messi brought the curtain down on his 21-year international career on Tuesday, bidding farewell to adoring Argentina fans in an emotional final appearance for the former world champions in Buenos Aires.
In a perfectly scripted finale, the 39-year-old widely regarded as the greatest football player in history signed off with his 126th international goal in front of 85,000 supporters as Argentina cruised to a 3-0 victory over Benin.
Messi, playing in his record-extending 208th international, also provided the assist for the opening goal scored by veteran Nicolas Otamendi, with Nico Paz also scoring.
But the match was a footnote to the occasion itself, which saw Messi savoring the adulation of the Monumental Stadium crowd one last time for an event which had been billed as 'The Last Tango'.
Beforehand, Messi wiped away tears as the bus carrying him and his Argentina team-mates made its way through crowds of wellwishers en route to the stadium.
Messi took the field alongside his three children and received affectionate waves from his wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, and his mother, Celia Cuccittini, who were watching from a VIP box.
Shortly before kick off, a giant Argentina jersey bearing the word "Gracias" (Thank You) above the football superstar's No.10 was laid out on the pitch as the crowd roared their approval.
Messi welled up again as Falklands War veteran Fabio Santana sang the national anthem beside a banner which read – "The Malvinas are Argentine" – the same banner held aloft by players after their 2-1 World Cup semi-final win over England.
The match was halted in the 10th minute – in tribute to Messi's famous shirt number – for a minute-long ovation to the former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain star.
He crowned the occasion with a goal from the penalty spot in the 71st minute.
[[nid:1549460]]
'Gave it my all'
At the final whistle a drone show lit up the night sky above the stadium, showing Messi's image and thanking the eight-time Ballon D'Or-winner for his career.
Messi's farewell came two and a half months after Argentina's World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey, where Messi exited in tears after making little impression in an ill-tempered 1-0 loss.
"I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance," Messi wrote at the time.
Before Tuesday's game, the University of Buenos Aires awarded Messi an honorary doctorate in a ceremony at the Argentine Football Association (AFA) headquarters.
Messi, who has in the past spoken of his regret at not studying more, expressed pride at the distinction.
"To be able to say that I am an honorary doctor!," he joked.
Outside the Argentina Football Association headquarters, fans unfurled a huge Argentine flag with his image inscribed "The joy of my life."
Former Barcelona team-mate Neymar paid tribute to the departing champion on X.
"It's not just Argentina that thanks you, the world thanks you for everything you did for football. Thank you for making me love football even more," he said.
Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated.
Messi's departure comes four years after his greatest triumph in international football, leading Argentina to victory at the 2022 World Cup to end the country's 36-year wait for a third title, cementing his status as Diego Maradona's heir.
"I believe Messi gave everything, absolutely everything, so it doesn't bother me at all that he's leaving. He has more than earned it, let him enjoy himself, let him rest," Cecilia Adriano, 52, told AFP.
During his time with the Albiceleste, Argentina won one World Cup, were runners-up twice (Brazil 2014 and North America 2026) and were also crowned Copa America champions in 2021 and 2024.

© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Immigration to rope in MCMC, CCID in Pahang scam centre probe
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department will work with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and police's Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) to investigate a foreign scam syndicate busted at a secluded resort in Sungai Lembing, Pahang.
Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said further investigations would focus on identifying the types of scams allegedly carried out from the call centre and determining the syndicate's wider operations.
"We will work with MCMC and CCID to investigate further and determine what types of scams were being carried out by this call centre," he said when contacted.
Zakaria said investigators would also determine whether any of the foreigners detained were themselves victims of job-scam syndicates and had been forced to work at the call centre.
"We also want to establish whether any of the suspects involved were victims of a job-scam syndicate who were forced to work for the syndicate," he said.
Zakaria said investigations also found that the syndicate was believed to have operated in two other countries before coming to Malaysia.
"Based on passport details, the members had been to Cambodia and Vietnam.
"They are believed to have been based in Cambodia for about nine months before they came to Malaysia," he said.
The syndicate's practice of moving between countries was believed to be part of efforts to avoid detection by local authorities.
Zakaria had said information contained in passports seized during the raid showed that some members had travelled to Cambodia and Vietnam.
"They would operate in one country for a certain period before moving to another country and operating there for another period.
"This could possibly be to prevent their activities from being detected by the authorities in the respective countries," he said.
A total of 98 people — 95 foreigners and three Malaysians — were detained when Immigration raided the
resort at Jalan Sungai Arang
on Oct 5 following about a month of intelligence gathering.
The foreigners comprised 88 Chinese nationals, two Myanmar nationals and one national each from Indonesia, Hong Kong, Vietnam, Cambodia and Russia.
Investigations also found that the syndicate was largely self-sufficient, with members believed to have remained within the resort while it was operating.
The syndicate even hired cooks to prepare meals for its members on the premises.
"We believe they only obtained their supplies from outside and the cooking was done inside the premises," he said.
The arrangement was among measures believed to have minimised the movement of syndicate members outside the resort and reduced the risk of drawing attention to their operations.
The resort had no electricity supply, with the syndicate relying on generators to power its operations.
Eleven Starlink sets believed to have provided internet connectivity were among the equipment seized during the raid.
The syndicate was also believed to have hired local lookouts to monitor movements into the secluded property.
It had been operating from the Sungai Lembing resort for about three months before it was busted.
Authorities also seized 100 mobile phones, 120 desktop computers, unused SIM cards and RM5,000 in cash.
The syndicate is believed to have operated around the clock, with members working in shifts and subjected to performance targets.
Preliminary investigations indicated that the call centre was being used for scam activities, with Chinese members believed to have targeted victims in China.
All those detained were taken to the Putrajaya Immigration Office for further investigation.

Title: Kota Baru man stabs nurse wife six times, remanded seven days
Article:
KOTA BARU: A nurse was seriously injured after being stabbed six times by her husband at their home in Kampung Padang Lepai near Kadok on Monday.
The 44-year-old victim, who suffered stab wounds to her body and neck, is receiving treatment at Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital.
Following the 8.38pm incident, police arrested the 47-year-old suspect to assist in the investigation.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Azmir Damiri said police received a report on the case on the same night.
He added that the suspect was detained after surrendering himself to police.
"Police have yet to establish the motive behind the incident.
"The suspect has been remanded for seven days from yesterday to assist in the investigation," he said when contacted.
Azmir said the case was being investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons.
Police also seized a vegetable knife from the suspect.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sunken Silk Road city reveals Central Asia's lost history
Article:
TORU-AYGYR: The sun had barely risen, but diver Elizaveta Bodrova was already raring to plunge into the cold waters of Lake Issyk-Kul, where the ruins of a once-thriving city have lain submerged for centuries.
Situated on an ancient trading route between China and Europe, little is known about the history of the settlement under Kyrgyzstan's largest lake or how it came to be flooded some 800 years ago.
Together with a team of around 20 scientists, Bodrova is helping uncover its past, findings that could shape our understanding of the history of Central Asia and beyond.
"The visibility isn't very good today, but I hope we'll still be able to find the boundary of the settlement," the 42-year-old volunteer told AFP with a smile, before hopping off a motorboat into the depths below.
The project, which began in 2024 and is funded by the Russian Academy of Sciences, is the first major exploration of the site since it was rediscovered in the 19th century.
[[nid:1549441]]
'Blind spot'
The settlement is located at the heart of what was once the Silk Road, a trading route that linked China to the Mediterranean from the 2nd century BC until the mid-15th century.
Although often associated with nomads, what is now Kyrgyzstan has been inhabited by multiple civilisations throughout its history, among them Turkic dynasties that traded between Europe and China.
"This is actually a blind spot in history, even though it is right in the centre of Central Asia," expedition director Maxim Menshikov, who was steering the boat, said of the ruins.
"It is a very important chapter in the history of humankind, because it was the period that linked East and West during the Middle Ages. The Silk Road is not merely the history of a single region, it is the history of Eurasia as a whole," he added.
The section of Silk Road that passed through the settlement during its existence is thought to have been under the control of the Karakhanids, a Turkic dynasty that controlled much of Central Asia from the 9th to early 13th centuries.
Researchers believe the city, the name and population of which are not known, may have covered up to five square kilometres (nearly two square miles).
Accurately dating the remains has been difficult.
But traces of two cemeteries discovered at the site suggest they were built during the early Islamisation of the region.
Among the discovered remains was a decorated public building, possibly a mosque, public bath or religious school.
[[nid:1549440]]
Like 'Pompeii'
After several hours scouring the bed of the salt lake, the divers returned to dry land with their spoils: The remains of animal bones and pottery shards.
"The bones that have been found will enable archaeologists to determine their diet and age of the remains, as well as the diet of the people who lived in this region," said Viktor Pozdnyakov, a diver and laboratory assistant on the expedition team.
"The pottery will enable us to date the finds and determine the approximate period more precisely. And, of course, to understand where it was produced, how and by what method," the 22-year-old added.
Back at base, the artefacts are carefully preserved, catalogued and recorded.
Among them was a child's chamber pot, known as a "tuvaq".
"These are still in use today in Central Asia and the Caucasus," said Menshikov, pointing to it as evidence of daily life in the city.
Although known to researchers since the 19th century, the site has only been systematically explored in recent years by Russian and Kyrgyz teams.
The researchers hope their work will improve understanding of Central Asian history.
"You could compare this research to that of Pompeii," said Menshikov, referring to the largely preserved ruins of an ancient Roman city near Naples buried by an eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD.
"They had a highly developed civilisation and culture. And in an instant, nature simply destroyed it all," he said.
What submerged the city under Issyk-Kul remains a mystery.
Among the theories is that the settlement sank to the bottom of the lake following a landslide, or that it was gradually flooded by a "tectonic dam" – a natural damming of a water body that could have occurred following an earthquake.
The probable cause was a "past seismic disaster", said Andrei Strelnikov, a geologist with the Russian Academy of Sciences.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lula campaign scrambles to rebrand before Brazil runoff
Article:
AFTER a bruising first round of Brazil's presidential election, President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is rushing to overhaul his campaign communications to engage millions of Brazilians who did not vote, according to people close to the campaign.
Lula finished nearly two percentage points — about 2.2 million votes — behind right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in Sunday's vote, making the three-term leftist the underdog in an Oct 25 runoff.
As markets cheered Bolsonaro's odds, Lula's allies met in Brasilia on Monday to regroup and plan a rebrand.
At the meeting, Lula pushed what is being dubbed internally the "fear strategy" to remind voters of the risks a Bolsonaro presidency he says would pose to popular social benefits.
People close to the campaign say Lula blames the messaging for failing to reach enough young people and women.
Some party figures point to Lula's social communications minister, Sidonio Palmeira, whose business partner Raul Rebelo runs the campaign's messaging, for pushing less accessible themes like sovereignty and critical minerals.
One TV campaign advert was devoted entirely to rare earths.
Rebelo is staying for now, but Otavio Antunes, a more aggressive strategist, is expected to join the national team, two people with the campaign said.
Lula's Workers' Party is courting the nine million-plus voters who backed minor candidates, but mainly targeting the record 33 million who abstained on Sunday, which it attributes to apathy rather than opposition to Lula.
A new Workers' Party social media ad warns that "some losses can't be undone," as slips of paper naming government programmes, including one sending doctors to remote areas and above-inflation pension increases, blow from an open hand.
Bolsonaro's press office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In a recent interview, he pledged to keep Bolsa Familia — Brazil's flagship cash-transfer program created by Lula — and let recipients stay on it even after finding formal work or starting a business.
With less than three weeks to go, campaign coordinator Paulo Okamoto said the campaign would build a network of left-leaning influencers to aid the social media push.
Lula himself could prove an obstacle. The 80-year-old does not carry a phone and often criticises screen culture.
While he promised Monday to make more social videos — which he calls "selfies" — Lula also said he wants to do more radio interviews before the runoff.
* The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal's grim DNA puzzle to identify flood dead
Article:
NUWAKOT: Clutching a photograph of his missing son, Rajesh Ram is pinning his hopes on DNA testing – like thousands of others desperately seeking relatives swept away by Nepal's catastrophic Himalayan floods.
"I searched for him everywhere, but I could not find his body," 53-year-old Ram told AFP, still waiting for answers about his son Suroj Kumar, a garage mechanic in Betrawati, which was swamped by the floods.
Nepal was overwhelmed by the sheer scale of destruction from the tsunami-like wall of freezing water and debris triggered by a glacial and rock collapse on the Nepal-China border on August 26.
The scale of the identification task is immense.
With thousands of DNA profiles to process, fragmented remains and limited technical capacity and manpower, experts warn matching bodies to families could take weeks.
Nepali disaster authorities have recovered 1,454 bodies – but around a third of those are only partial remains.
Just 112 bodies have been identified and returned to their families. A further 5,285 people are missing in Nepal, including hundreds of foreigners.
In China, the toll is 43 dead and 519 missing, according to state media – taking the combined toll to nearly 1,500 dead and 5,800 missing.
At Nepal's two forensic laboratories, both in Kathmandu, experts are working to profile samples and build a database on a scale they have never handled before.
"In a year we would analyse 1,000 to 1,500 samples, often in case of paternity or crime scenes," said Mukul Pradhan, chief scientific officer at the National Forensic Science Laboratory. "We are now processing thousands of samples."
[[nid:1549434]]
'Pain'
A total of 3,685 forensic samples are undergoing DNA testing, including more than 1,300 collected from recovered bodies.
Blood samples are easier to profile, but those taken from teeth or bones can take several days to process.
Nepal has buried more than 1,200 bodies, carefully numbering and tagging them so they can be retrieved if a DNA match is found.
"A large number of people are missing, and the bodies that have been found are difficult to identify," said Nepali police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle. "We understand the pain people are in, and our teams are working diligently."
Some bodies were carried far downstream by the floodwaters, further complicating the task, said Nirajan Thapa, Chief of Biology section at the National Forensic Science Laboratory.
"In an earthquake or an accident, people are recovered in a specific area, so we work in a closed scenario – the body's DNA has to be compared to a limited number of samples," Thapa said. "But that scale has now become very large."
DNA alone cannot identify a body without a reference sample from a relative.
"Just by extracting a DNA profile is not enough to identify someone," Thapa said. "We have to extract a DNA profile from their relatives and then compare."
That means authorities must process samples from both unidentified remains and thousands of relatives before they can establish matches.
Several countries have sent in support teams, including neighbouring India and China, as well as South Korea. Fingerprint experts from the United States and Singapore are also assisting.
Thapa said that with that help, matching could begin within a few weeks.
But until the results come, the families behind those samples face a painful limbo. Some families have held symbolic cremation funerals for the missing.
Ram wonders if he will ever get any answers. "I am waiting (to see) if I can find any remains of my son," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four terrace houses damaged in early morning Prai fire
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: Four terrace houses were damaged in a fire at Taman Senangin early today.
Fortunately, all 10 occupants, including eight senior citizens, managed to escape.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the fire broke out at the four terrace houses, including one that was unoccupied, shortly after midnight.
Damages were estimated at between 30 per cent and 80 per cent at the affected houses.
"The occupants of all the affected houses managed to escape before firefighters arrived. No injuries or fatalities were reported," he said.
He said the department received a distress call at 12.45am.
A total of 24 firefighters from the Prai, Butterworth, Bandar Perda and Kepala Batas fire stations, assisted by the Chain Ferry volunteer fire brigade, were involved in the operation.
The fire was brought under control at 1.23am and fully extinguished at 1.48am, with mopping-up work carried out to ensure there were no remaining hazards.
The operation ended at 2.29am and the case was handed over to the Fire Investigation Team for further action.
Police and Tenaga Nasional Bhd also assisted at the scene.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pas: Viral candidate list for Melaka polls not official
Article:
MELAKA: A list of Pas candidates for four state seats in the upcoming state election that went viral on social media is not official, the party said.
Melaka Pas said its circulation could confuse the public.
It said the circulation of the list could confuse the public and clarified that several social media pages carrying party-related content, including TV Pas Melaka and Melaka Kini, are not under the supervision or management of the state party leadership.
The party also reminded its members and supporters not to use the pages as official sources of reference to avoid confusion and the spread of inaccurate information.
"The public is advised not to believe or spread unverified information," it said in a statement.
Meanwhile, former Bukit Katil seat candidate Mohammad Al Hafiz Yahya, when contacted, said he was also unaware of the list and had not received any confirmation regarding his candidacy.
He said any decision on the candidates would have to await a decision by Pas central leadership and that he did not want to pre-empt any official party announcement.
"So far, there has been no confirmation and I myself do not know where the source of the information came from.
Earlier, a Facebook post went viral featuring a list of candidates proposed by Pas to contest four state seats in the Melaka election.
It claimed that Zulhilmi Suboh or Nor Faizal Nordin had been nominated to contest for the Bemban seat, Al Hafiz Yahya for Bukit Katil, a candidate from the Melaka Pas Youth Council for Ayer Keroh and Bakri Jamaluddin for Paya Rumput.

Title: Brazil coffee exports hit 20-month high in September
Article:
SAO PAULO: Brazil's green coffee exports in September totaled 235,800 metric tons, or 3.93 million 60-kg bags, the highest volume in 20 months, according to government data published on Tuesday.
Brazil's exports jumped 20.4 per cent compared to the same period in 2025
Brazil is exporting volumes from a projected record crop, whose harvesting work had been delayed due to rains
Revenue from the coffee exports totaled $1.29 billion in September, up 8.7 per cent year-on-year, with the higher volumes more than offsetting a 9.8 per cent drop in the average price
Brazil is the largest exporter and producer of coffee

Title: AI borrowing binge rattles US markets
Article:
NEW YORK: The world's richest companies can no longer rely on their massive cash piles alone to stay in the artificial intelligence race and have suddenly started borrowing massively in a shift that is sending repercussions across the world.
Rising US interest rates, including on the Treasury bonds that anchor the global economy, are sending tremors through the financial world, and some analysts point to the AI borrowing bonanza as one of the culprits.
From next to nothing in 2024, tech sector borrowing has reached around US$500 billion in the nine months since January, as Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft and others raise debt handover first to finance the chips, servers and data centres that power AI.
Goldman Sachs expects a further ramp-up in 2027 to US$1.2 trillion.
"This is not something that we've seen before," said James Vrachas, executive director in charge of acquisitions at fundraising advisory firm Post Oak Group, who estimates that AI now accounts for 25 per cent of all corporate bond issuance, up from four per cent two years ago.
In inflation-adjusted terms, the AI sector is expected to borrow more this year than US cable operators did to build out the entire internet, or than railroad companies did during the 19th-century US rail boom.
So far, investors have eagerly snapped up the chance to lend to the tech giants, but they have demanded returns that would have been unthinkable for such blue-chip companies not long ago.
Even Meta has had to offer more than 7 per cent a year, while riskier cloud data center specialists have gone above 9 per cent.
The impact reaches well beyond the companies building AI – their debt is even starting to crowd out demand for the US government bonds that anchor the financial system.
An investor who might otherwise buy a US Treasury bond "might decide to buy Microsoft" instead, said Mark Malek, chief investment officer at Siebert Financial, referring to the tech giant's bonds.
That shift pushes up the rates Washington pays to borrow, he explained.
This adds to the other force driving up US borrowing costs: inflation, fuelled by the war against Iran and high energy prices.
The interest rate on 10-year US government bonds – Wall Street's benchmark and widely seen as the most important number in global finance, setting the tone for everything from mortgages to car loans – is now above 5.30 per cent, its highest level since 2002.
- 'Sharper correction' -
Adding to the volatility, hedge funds had piled into US government bonds like never before, holding 7 per cent of all those in circulation at the end of 2025, though that share has since fallen.
Hedge funds, which place big bets on markets, move their money far faster than more cautious investors such as insurers and pension funds.
Even if the war and the oil situation stabilised, Vrachas said, "I wouldn't expect the yields to dramatically reduce, to be honest, because of this influence of the AI debt situation."
Beyond the rising cost of borrowing, some are questioning the risks of betting on an AI boom that could hit a wall, as the dot-com bubble did in 2000.
Even a moderate slowdown in the frenzied pace of construction, delays on certain projects or weaker-than-expected revenue growth could trigger a shock in financial markets, Malek warned.
In late September, the Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee warned that "the risk of a sharper correction persists", particularly if concerns about the pace of AI development or adoption hit earnings expectations.
In July, amid some second-guessing about the AI boom, the tech-heavy Nasdaq index fell nearly 7 per cent.
Against this backdrop, cloud specialist Oracle is sometimes seen as a bellwether.
With massive debt (US$125 billion), cash reserves that shrink every quarter and a possible delay on a huge data center project in New Mexico, several warning lights are flashing for Larry Ellison's group.
"Let's say Oracle has a problem... They can't pay for something," Malek said. Trouble with its debt "could trigger contagion" across AI finance as a whole, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US luxury spending slows ahead of midterms, credit card data shows
Article:
PARIS: US credit card spending on luxury brands fell for a third consecutive month in September, retail lender Citi said on Tuesday, signalling further weakness in the industry's biggest market as the US heads into the November 3 midterm elections.
Buffeted by prolonged weakness in China and the economic fallout of the Iran war, luxury brands have pinned hopes on resilient demand from wealthy US shoppers, including a growing cohort of AI millionaires, to offset softer sales elsewhere and help lift the sector out of a prolonged downturn.
While continued wealth growth among affluent consumers supported the top-end of the market in September, overall US luxury credit card purchases fell 6.0 per cent from a year earlier, after declining 4.0 per cent in both July and August, Citi analysts said in a research note.
The luxury brands most exposed to the US include Tapestry , owner of Coach and Kate Spade; French conglomerate LVMH , known for brands like Louis Vuitton and Tiffany; and Italy's Ferragamo, they said.
Still "brands with greater exposure to higher-end consumers should remain relatively resilient, supported by equity-market wealth effects," Citi said.
Spending on leather goods and ready-to-wear items improved sequentially in September, the note added, while watches and luxury jewellery deteriorated even further.
Most soft luxury brands which sell apparel, shoes and leather goods have raised their prices by low single digits in percentage terms so far this year, slightly below the low to mid-single-digit price increases from watch and jewellery makers, the note said.
A COOLING ECONOMY
The Citi data, based on millions of credit card transactions, follows surveys from the Conference Board and the University of Michigan that showed growing unease about the US economy ahead of the midterm elections, when voters will decide control of Congress.
The run-up to elections is often marked by heightened caution among consumers and businesses as political uncertainty weighs on spending decisions. Economists say rising US Treasury yields and mortgage rates could further cool economic activity.
Morgan Stanley analysts said in September that the downturn in US luxury spending leaves brands with little scope to deliver the long-awaited return to growth after two consecutive years of contraction.
The brokerage expects luxury groups to flag weaker US demand during the upcoming earnings season, which begins on October 12 when LVMH, widely seen as a bellwether for the industry, reports third-quarter sales.
Gucci owner Kering, which releases earnings on October 22, told analysts last week to expect a slowdown in the US market, according to Italian brokerage Equita.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japan's real wages rise for eighth straight month in August
Article:
TOKYO: Japan's real wages rose 1.5 per cent in August from a year earlier, marking the eighth consecutive month of gains, government data showed on Wednesday, pointing to a continued recovery in wage growth.
The solid wage data supports the case for the Bank of Japan to continue raising interest rates after hiking its benchmark rate last month.
The growth in real pay was slower than July's revised 2.0 per cent gain.
Average nominal wages, or total cash earnings, rose 3.8 per cent to 311,364 yen (US$1,969.66), slower than a revised 4.3 per cent increase in July.
Workers' base salaries, or regular pay, increased 3.8 per cent, unchanged from a revised 3.8 per cent rise in July. Overtime pay growth in August stood at 5.2 per cent, up from July's revised 4.5 per cent rise.
Special payments, consisting mostly of one-time bonuses that tend to be volatile, showed no growth in August after a revised 5.3 per cent increase in July.
The inflation rate used by the ministry to calculate the headline real wage indicator remained unchanged from July at 2.2 per cent. It remained below year-earlier levels, when it stood at 3.1 per cent.
Annual core inflation in Japan's capital accelerated in September at its fastest pace in 10 months, data showed last week, highlighting mounting price pressures and bolstering the case for further interest rate hikes from the central bank.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dewan Rakyat: Sick projects, P. Ramlee works' copyright among issues in focus today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Strengthening contractor selection and performance assessment criteria to address delays in government projects and 'sick projects' is among the key issues to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper on the official Parliament website, Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (PN-Langkawi) will ask the works minister about proactive measures to address weaknesses in contractors' management and financial capabilities, as well as new mechanisms to be introduced.
The latest developments on the proposed Parental Care Bill will also be raised by Rodiyah Sapiee (GPS-Batang Sadong), who will ask the women, family and community development minister about the status of the bill.
She will also seek clarification on the form and mechanism of comprehensive social protection expected to be announced to safeguard the welfare of senior citizens amid the country's demographic shift towards an ageing population.
Meanwhile, Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson) will ask the Education Minister to elaborate on the ministry's preparedness to accommodate the simultaneous increase in six- and seven-year-old children entering Year One for the 2027 school session.
The preservation of artistic heritage will also be raised by Onn Abu Bakar (PH-Batu Pahat), who will ask the communications minister to provide an update on government initiatives to acquire or repurchase ownership and copyright rights, as well as management rights, to films by the late Tan Sri P. Ramlee for preservation as national heritage assets.
Following the oral question-and-answer session, the sitting will continue with the tabling of a motion by the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department on the Auditor-General's Report 2/2026, which was tabled last Monday.
The motion, among other things, calls on all relevant ministries, departments and agencies to examine the findings and recommendations of the audit report objectively to strengthen governance integrity and the management of public funds.
The sitting is also scheduled to continue with the second reading of the Food (Amendment) Bill 2026 by the health minister.
The Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, which began last Monday, is scheduled to run for 37 days until Dec 8.
