Title: Immigration to get real-time data access under NIISe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department will have access to real-time data sharing with multiple government agencies under the National Integrated Immigration System (NIISe), Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said.
He said NIISe would gradually replace the existing Malaysian Immigration System (myIMMs), with improvements including enhanced early screening, traveller risk profiling, and real-time data integration and sharing.
"These include the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN), the police, Interpol, Inland Revenue Board (IRB), Prisons Department and Transport Ministry," he said in a written reply in response to a question from Rushdan Rusmi (PN-Padang Besar).
Saifuddin said the government currently implemented real-time data sharing and integration through myIMMs, an integrated information system supporting the Immigration Department's core operations.
He said myIMMs was used for immigration control and checks at the country's entry points, including checking travellers' or high-risk individuals' travel documents against Interpol databases.
"To modernise and improve the efficiency of control at entry points, improvements and modernisation of the system are continuously being implemented," he said.
He said the government was also developing the National Border Control System (SKSN) as a long-term plan to strengthen the country's border security ecosystem.
He said SKSN would be equipped with advanced surveillance systems based on artificial intelligence (AI) and data analytics to enable unmanned operations, rapid real-time information dissemination and continuous surveillance of Malaysia's land and maritime borders.
"The system is a plan by the ministry and efforts are still ongoing to refine its details," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man killed as 4WD plunges into 100m ravine in Gua Musang
Article:
KOTA BARU: A man was killed when the four-wheel-drive (4WD) vehicle he was driving skidded before plunging into a ravine about 100m deep at Jalan Ladang Pos Pulat in Gua Musang.
The vehicle and victim were found two days after the incident.
Gua Musang police chief superintendent Sik Choon Foo said police received a report from the public at 4.30pm yesterday about the discovery of the Toyota Hilux at the bottom of the ravine, with the victim found unconscious and pronounced dead at the scene.
He said preliminary investigations found that the accident was believed to have occurred on Sunday.
"Based on information from the victim's wife, the victim's last live location was detected on Sunday afternoon in the vicinity of the incident.
"On Oct 6, the victim's colleague went to the location of the last live location to search for him before finding the victim's Toyota Hilux at the bottom of the ravine," he said in a statement today.
Sik said investigations found that the victim was believed to have been driving his vehicle when it skidded into the ravine while going downhill.
He said no one was believed to have witnessed the incident, resulting in the vehicle driven by the victim going unnoticed by members of the public until it was found by his colleague.
The victim's body was subsequently brought up from the scene with the assistance of personnel from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department before being sent to the Forensic Unit of Gua Musang Hospital for a post-mortem.
"The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for the offence of reckless or dangerous driving resulting in death.
"Further investigations are still being conducted to identify the actual cause of the accident and the circumstances that led to the incident," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EC meeting today to set dates for Melaka polls
Article:
MELAKA: The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting today to fix the key dates for the 16th Melaka state election.
The meeting will be chaired by EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun, followed by a press conference scheduled at 11.30am to announce the decisions.
Among the matters to be determined are the election writ date, nomination day, early voting day and polling day, as well as the electoral roll.
The election arrangements are also expected to include the use of nomination centres and polling centres, as well as preparations for election personnel to ensure the voting process runs smoothly.
The
dissolution of the state assembly
on Sept 23 paved the way for an election to be held within 60 days.
With 28 seats up for contest, the state election will not only determine who forms the state government but will also be an important test of the actual strength of political blocs following major changes to the national political landscape since the 2021 Melaka state election.
In terms of voter numbers, Melaka is now vastly different from the state election five years ago.
As at April 20, 2026, the number of registered voters in Melaka stood at 683,543, an increase of 188,348, or about 38 per cent, from the 495,195 voters in the 2021 state election.
The addition of nearly 190,000 voters means this state election has a different demographic dimension.
New voters, including those automatically registered following the implementation of Undi18, could be a determining factor, particularly in seats previously won by narrow majorities.
The figure could also change further when the EC finalises the electoral roll.
The August 2026 Supplementary Electoral Roll alone contains 43,309 citizens aged 18 and above who were automatically registered as new voters, in addition to 34,411 voters who changed their constituencies and 2,728 who changed their voter category or status.
It will not only determine the overall number of voters but also provide a clearer picture of the size of the electoral field each party will face across the 28 state constituencies.
In the 2021 polls, BN won 21 state seats, while five were won by Pakatan Harapan (PH) and two by Perikatan Nasional (PN).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Paramount completes Warner Bros takeover, creating Skydance
Article:
LOS ANGELES: Paramount on Tuesday completed its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, uniting two of Hollywood's most storied studios in a media empire spanning television, news and cinema under the control of David Ellison.
The combined company, renamed Skydance, brings together Paramount Pictures and Warner Bros. Pictures, the CBS News and CNN networks, and the HBO and CBS television brands.
Ellison plans to eventually merge the Paramount+ and HBO Max streaming services.
"Today is a historic day, not just for Skydance but for our entire industry," said Ellison, while a company memo warned that layoffs could be in store.
His ultra-wealthy family's ties to US President Donald Trump have raised concerns among critics that the new Hollywood giant will toe the White House line in its news coverage.
"It's going to be a great company," Trump told reporters Tuesday as he left the White House.
Layoffs loom
The sprawling new corporation faces considerable challenges, with the entertainment industry in flux as streaming services and YouTube draw viewers away from traditional TV and movie theatre audiences dwindle.
Skydance shares ended their first day trading down 2.7 per cent on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker "SKYD."
The deal closed less than a week after a federal judge in California approved a settlement between Paramount and 12 US states that had sued to block the transaction on antitrust grounds.
Paramount won a bidding war against Netflix in February for Warner Bros. Discovery, and the Trump administration approved the deal, one of the largest-ever media mergers, in June without demanding a change to its business.
Skydance, which will have nearly US$70 billion in annual revenue, said it is targeting more than US$6 billion in cost savings within three years.
Ellison will serve as chairman and chief executive officer, with former Mattel chief Ynon Kreiz as co-CEO in charge of day-to-day operations and integrating the two businesses.
In a memo to the company's staff, titled "Day 1," Ellison and Kreiz said the merger "will bring change, including difficult decisions that affect our workforce."
"We are committed to handling this process thoughtfully and respectfully," said the memo seen by AFP.
The deal was backed by US$47 billion in new equity led by the Ellison family, private equity firm RedBird Capital and the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.
Ellison's father, billionaire Oracle founder Larry Ellison, provided major funding and a guarantee to lenders backing the deal.
The Ellison family holds the largest equity stake in Skydance.
Opponents in the movie industry said the combined company would slash jobs in a Hollywood already under pressure and reduce the number of films produced every year, while news media groups feared CNN's independence could be compromised.
The settlement with the states includes several safeguards on these issues, including a board meant to protect CNN's editorial independence.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FT Minister: Cabinet to be briefed on findings from vagrancy, child welfare ops
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said findings from integrated operations to address vagrancy and children in the capital will be presented to the Cabinet to seek more comprehensive solutions.
She said the KL Strike Force operation to address vagrancy and children, conducted early this morning, aimed to identify current trends, including hard-core cases involving individuals repeatedly detected in previous operations.
“We will present the findings to the Cabinet later to find a solution. We will have a team study the data first to see how many people have been detained repeatedly,” she told reporters after participating in the operation around the capital.
Also present were Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Datuk Lo Su Fui, Kuala Lumpur mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud and Federal Territories Department (JWP) director-general Datuk Muhammad Azmi Mohd Zain.
The integrated operation involved the Ministry of Health (MOH), National Registration Department (NRD), Immigration Department, Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL), Social Welfare Department (JKM), National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) and National Security Council (MKN).
Hannah said the operation was the third conducted in Kuala Lumpur this year, while the data collected would be compared with statistics from the past two years to formulate a more effective action plan.
She said the government would also hold further discussions with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) active in fieldwork to obtain their feedback and views.
According to Hannah, following the screening process, non-citizens or undocumented individuals would be handled by the Immigration Department; cases involving mental health issues would be referred to MOH, individuals who tested positive for drugs handed over to AADK, while Malaysians without a place to stay would be assisted by JKM and DBKL.
Touching on mental health cases, she acknowledged that the lack of dedicated facilities had resulted in some individuals returning to the streets after receiving treatment and creating a seemingly endless cycle.
Hannah said the operation was also important to safeguard the country’s image in conjunction with Visit Malaysia 2026, particularly in tourist hotspots such as Bukit Bintang.
In addition, Hannah said her ministry supported efforts by the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development to formulate a new law to strengthen JKM’s legal authority in handling cases involving individuals from various backgrounds. — Bernama

Title: Sexual harassment probe continues after motivational speaker released on bail
Article:
KANGAR, Oct 7 —A motivational speaker, who was remanded for two days to assist investigations into an alleged sexual harassment case, was released on police bail at about 5.30 pm today.
Perlis police chief DCP Hamzah Hashim said in a brief statement to Bernama that the investigation papers had been referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor for further instructions.
The media reported yesterday that the 33-year-old man had been remanded for two days from Monday to assist investigations into a police report filed against him in the district on Oct 3.
Earlier, the media reported on Sunday that police had received another report against the man.
Hamzah was quoted as saying the police report involved a 19-year-old female complainant, and the case was being investigated under Section 509 of the Penal Code, Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act.
The man was remanded for two days from Saturday in connection with a police report in Padang Besar, then released on police bail and rearrested by police from the Kangar District Police Headquarters for further action. — Bernama

Title: Terengganu student killed in three-bike crash
Article:
KUALA NERUS, Oct 7 —A 16-year-old student was killed while his younger sister was injured in a collision involving three motorcycles at Jalan Sungai Buaya, Kampung Batin, Seberang Takir here this afternoon.
Kuala Terengganu district police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the victim, Ahmad Areesy Zafreen Ahmad Azhar, died at the scene from serious injuries to several parts of his body.
He said the incident is believed to have occurred at about 5.10 pm when the victim, who was riding a Modenas Kriss from Kampung Batin towards Seberang Takir, overtook a vehicle before colliding with a Honda EX5 travelling in the opposite direction.
“The EX5, ridden by an 18-year-old male teenager, was then hit from behind by another motorcycle travelling in the same direction.
“Both motorcycle riders were injured and sent to Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital (HSNZ) for treatment. The victim’s younger sister, who was riding pillion on his motorcycle, was also sent to the same hospital for treatment,” he said in a statement today.
Azli said the victim, a student of Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Bukit Tunggal, was taken to the HSNZ Forensic Department for further action, while the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: Schools, kindergartens and childcare centres in Batu Pahat to close amid hazardous air quality
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Oct 7 — All schools, kindergartens and childcare centres across the Batu Pahat district have been ordered to close from tomorrow, Oct 7, after the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeded 200, reaching the “very unhealthy” level.
In a statement today, the Batu Pahat District Disaster Management Committee said the district’s API reading reached 203 as of 8pm.
It said the closures were ordered under the National Haze Action Plan and Ministry of Education (MOE) guidelines to safeguard students’ and school staff’s health and safety.
“Schools must conduct home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) if instructed to do so by the MOE, the Johor Education Department (JPNJ) or the Batu Pahat District Education Office (PPD), subject to the applicable directives and guidelines.
“Schools must also inform parents or guardians of the arrangements for the PdPR, students’ assignments and communication channels through the schools’ official channels,” it said.
According to the statement, any decision on reopening the schools will be based on the latest air quality readings and directives from the authorities.
The committee also advised the public to obtain information through the official channels of the Department of Environment, MOE, JPNJ, Batu Pahat PPD and Batu Pahat District Office, and to avoid sharing unverified information. — Bernama

Title: Fish deaths in Sungai Perak under investigation, says state exco
Article:
IPOH, Oct 7 —The Department of Environment (DOE) is gathering evidence and conducting sample-matching tests to determine the actual cause of a fish die-off in Sungai Perak near Sayong, Kuala Kangsar recently.
Perak Science, Environment and Green Technology Committee chairman Teh Kok Lim said the state government did not rule out the possibility that the incident was caused by waste discharged from a nearby palm oil mill, but a DOE investigation was necessary to establish the cause.
“We suspect (the palm oil mill waste discharge), but there must be strong evidence before the matter can be brought to court.
“For now, DOE is conducting an investigation and we expect findings on the incident to be obtained soon,” he told reporters after attending the Perak Innovation Convention 2026 at Stadium Indera Mulia here today.
Previously, social media posts went viral showing various species of fish, including tengalan, baung and patin, dead at the location, raising concerns among netizens about water pollution that could affect the ecosystem and the livelihoods of inland fishermen. — Bernama

Title: Smoggy start to the day: Batu Pahat tops API at 197, with Selangor, KL and Putrajaya also unhealthy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Batu Pahat recorded the country’s highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 197 at 9am today as unhealthy air quality persisted across parts of Malaysia.
The latest Department of Environment data showed 32 of its 68 monitoring stations in the unhealthy category at 9.07am, while 25 stations recorded moderate air quality and two recorded good air quality.
Johor accounted for several of the highest readings, with Tangkak at 172, Segamat and Pasir Gudang at 171 each, and Kluang at 167.
In Selangor, Johan Setia recorded an API of 190, followed by Shah Alam at 180, Petaling Jaya and Banting at 176 each, and Klang at 169.
In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras recorded 189 while another monitoring station in the Federal Territory recorded 177.
Putrajaya recorded an API of 187.
Negeri Sembilan also saw elevated readings, with Nilai at 189, Seremban at 181 and Port Dickson at 169.
In Melaka, Bukit Rambai recorded 175, while Alor Gajah and Bandaraya Melaka each recorded 174.
Elsewhere, Temerloh recorded 168, Indera Mahkota in Kuantan 160 and Jerantut 159 in Pahang, while Tasek Ipoh recorded 174 and Tanjong Malim 154 in Perak.
In Terengganu, Kemaman and Paka each recorded 156, while Tawau recorded 155 in Sabah.
Air quality in Sarawak remained in the good category based on the readings supplied.
Under the API classification, readings from 101 to 200 are considered unhealthy, while 51 to 100 is moderate and 0 to 50 is good.
No monitoring stations were recording very unhealthy or hazardous air quality in the 9.07am update.

Title: Man dies after 4WD plunges 100 metres into ravine, found two days later
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 7 —A local man was killed after the four-wheel-drive (4WD) vehicle he was driving is believed to have skidded before plunging into a ravine about 100 metres deep at Jalan Ladang Pos Pulat, in Gua Musang. The vehicle and victim were only found two days after the incident.
Gua Musang police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said police received a report from a member of the public at 4.30 pm yesterday about the discovery of the Toyota Hilux at the bottom of the ravine, with the victim found unconscious and pronounced dead at the scene.
He said preliminary investigations found that the accident was believed to have occurred last Sunday, two days before the vehicle and victim were found.
“Based on information from the victim’s wife, the victim’s last live location was detected on Sunday afternoon in the vicinity of the incident.
“On Oct 6, the victim’s colleague went to the location of the last live location to search for him before finding the victim’s Toyota Hilux at the bottom of the ravine,” he said in a statement today.
Sik said investigations found that the victim was believed to have been driving his vehicle when it skidded into the ravine while going downhill.
He said no one was believed to have witnessed the incident, resulting in the vehicle driven by the victim going unnoticed by members of the public until it was found by his colleague.
The victim’s body was subsequently brought up from the scene with the assistance of personnel from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department before being sent to the Forensic Unit of Gua Musang Hospital for a post-mortem.
“The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for the offence of reckless or dangerous driving resulting in death.
“Further investigations are still being conducted to identify the actual cause of the accident and the circumstances that led to the incident,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Unity Ministry confirms national harmony commission will not be established
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 —The Ministry of National Unity (KPN) has decided against establishing the National Harmony Commission (SKN), following a decision by the National Unity Advisory Council at its first meeting of 2026.
In a written reply published on the Parliament website, the ministry said the decision followed two engagement sessions and considered the views of all parties.
“The engagement sessions involved civil society organisations, government agencies, academics, community leaders and various stakeholders to assess the need for, scope and implications of establishing the commission, as well as the challenges and feasibility involved,” the ministry said.
It was responding to a question from Dr V. Sivakumar (PH-Batu Gajah), who asked about the status and timeline for establishing SKN, its proposed enforcement powers, and assurances that it would not duplicate the roles of existing agencies in addressing discrimination and racial tensions.
As such, the ministry will focus on strengthening existing institutions, namely the Department of National Unity and Integration (JPNIN), neighbourhood watch area (KRT) communities and community mediators, as the lead agencies for managing social harmony, in what it sees as a practical, responsive and cost-effective approach.
It also said the decision will avoid duplicating existing agencies’ functions and the costs of setting up a new entity.
At the same time, the ministry can leverage the existing structures, networks and mechanisms developed by JPNIN through KRTs, community mediators, the Community Sensitive Issues Reference Centre (PRISMA), the e-Sepakat system (for managing unity issues), the National Public Community Complaints Network (RAKAN), and its network of unity officers at state and district levels. — Bernama

Title: Residents in Lahad Datu, Tawau feel tremors from 5.0-magnitude quake
Article:
LAHAD DATU, Oct 7 — The 5.0-magnitude earthquake that struck the waters off Sandakan at 9.11 pm last night was felt by residents in Lahad Datu and Tawau, with several describing brief but noticeable tremors.
Nurse Nur Damia Hanafi, 34, from Lahad Datu, said she felt the shaking while on her way home.
“I was stopped at a red light when I suddenly felt the car shaking.
“I thought someone was shaking the car from outside, but the tremor lasted only briefly. I continued my journey home and only later found out that an earthquake had occurred,” she told Bernama.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the epicentre was located about 48 kilometres east of Lahad Datu, at coordinates 4.9 degrees North and 118.7 degrees East, at a depth of 10 kilometres.
Public servant Norusidah Ruslan, 45, also from Lahad Datu, said she noticed the tremor while working on diamond embroidery and saw the embroidered clothes hanging nearby sway.
“I thought I was feeling dizzy, but when I saw the clothes moving, I realised the shaking was getting stronger.
“This was my first experience of an earthquake. I panicked and called my husband, who was at a friend’s house, to check on his safety and ask whether the tremor had been felt elsewhere,” she said.
Housewife Nur Medina Abdullah, 40, said she was cleaning the kitchen when she felt the shaking for several seconds.
“At first I thought I was dizzy. I even wondered if there was something supernatural because I was alone in the kitchen. It turned out to be the tremor,” said the Lahad Datu resident
The tremor was also felt in Tawau.
E-hailing driver Muhd Andri Sapar, 35, said he felt the tremor for about eight seconds while having a drink with a friend at a hotel in the town.
“The tremor felt strong but was brief. I was sitting and chatting with my friend when suddenly everything started to sway and the water in the glass was sloshing,” he said.
Housewife Siti Amilah Terence, 35, said she and her husband also experienced the tremor while leaving a mobile phone shop in Tawau.
“We felt the movement but it did not last long. I felt unsteady and dizzy during the tremor,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan records RM41.5b in approved investments until June 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — A total of RM41.5 billion in investments were approved for Negeri Sembilan from 2023 to June 2026 under the purview of the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) and the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida), with the potential to create 14,953 job opportunities.
Miti said domestic investments accounted for RM24.2 billion, or 58 per cent, while foreign investments amounted to RM17.3 billion, or 42 per cent.
The manufacturing sector was the largest contributor, with RM22 billion in investments, or 53 per cent. This was followed by the services sector with RM19.5 billion (46.9 per cent) and the primary sector with RM670,000 (0.1 per cent), Miti said in a written reply on the Parliament website today.
Miti was responding to Cha Kee Chin’s (PH-Rasah), who wanted to know Negeri Sembilan’s approved domestic and foreign investments from 2023 to 2026, the investment value, the number of job opportunities created, and the government’s measures to ensure that those residing in the Rasah parliamentary constituency will benefit from the investments.
Miti also said the federal government, together with Mida, the Negeri Sembilan state government, and relevant agencies, has continued to implement an integrated approach to ensure approved investments contribute to the state’s economic growth and benefit the local population.
Measures include increasing employment opportunities for locals through new investment projects, expansion, and diversification, particularly in the manufacturing and services sectors, including high-skilled jobs.
Companies implementing investment projects are also encouraged to prioritise the recruitment and development of the local workforce in line with their skills requirements.
The government also encourages collaboration between industries and technical and vocational education and training (TVET) institutions, higher education institutions and talent development agencies to ensure that the skills of the local workforce align with industry requirements.
These efforts are further strengthened through vendor development programmes, business matching and supply chain programmes to increase local companies’ participation, including small and medium enterprises (SMEs), as suppliers of products and services to companies investing in Negeri Sembilan, Miti said.
The government also encourages investors to obtain support services from the local business community, including in logistics, mechanical maintenance and construction, to ensure that SMEs are involved directly in the investment value chain.
To ensure that quality investments generate greater added value, the government has emphasised investments involving technology, automation, digitalisation, research and development (R&D) activities, as well as high-skilled jobs.
“This approach aims to ensure that the employment opportunities created not only increase in quantity but also offer better career prospects, skills enhancement and income opportunities for the local population,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Police rule out Malaysia as origin of private jet in Laos meth bust
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The seizure of 521 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine aboard a private jet in Laos on Oct 1 did not originate from Malaysia, but was instead suspected to be smuggled from that country to the Philippines.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said based on information from Laotian authorities, the chartered aircraft departed from Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang to Luang Prabang without carrying any cargo.
He said the flight from Subang carried only three individuals comprising a Singaporean pilot, a Malaysian co-pilot, and a Filipino passenger.
“The seized drugs were meant for the Manila market in the Philippines and not the Malaysian market. The aircraft departed from Subang Airport without any cargo before it was believed to have been used to transport the drug shipment from Laos to Manila,” he said in a statement here tonight.
Elaborating on the timeline shared by Laotian authorities, he said the private aircraft arrived at Luang Prabang International Airport at about 11.30 am local time on Oct 1.
“At 1.30 pm, two vehicles arrived at the airport area, and several airport staff subsequently assisted in transferring 23 bags from the vehicles onto trolleys to be loaded onto the aircraft.
“An inspection of all 23 bags uncovered 500 packages of drugs suspected to be methamphetamine weighing 521 kg,” he said.
Following the successful operation by Laotian authorities, a total of 13 individuals were arrested, including the three crew members and passenger who had departed from Subang.
Also arrested were 10 Laotian nationals, comprising three airport ground handling service staff and seven personnel operating X-ray scanning machines, with all suspects currently held in custody for further investigation by the country’s authorities.
Following this, Hussein said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) has launched a comprehensive investigation and will send NCID officers to Laos in the near future to record statements from the suspects.
“This move aims to obtain further information regarding the drug syndicate involved, particularly (on the possible involvement of syndicate members) in Malaysia,” he said.
The latest official statement clarifies the situation, following initial reports linking the arrival of the aircraft from Malaysia to the discovery of the drugs worth millions of ringgit. — Bernama

Title: Authorities believe 4WD involved in Johor Bahru mall fire (VIDEO)
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 7 — A fire at the basement car park of a shopping mall here this afternoon is believed to have involved a four-wheel-drive (4WD) vehicle, amid speculation on social media that the incident was linked to an electric vehicle (EV).
Larkin Fire and Rescue Station chief Mohd Suhaimi Abdul Jamal said the department received an emergency call at 3.40 pm, with fire engines arriving at the scene six minutes later.
He said 52 personnel from the Larkin, Tebrau and Kempas Fire and Rescue stations, Ulu Tiram Volunteer Fire Brigade and the mall’s Emergency Response Team (ERT) were involved in the operation.
“Of the 11 vehicles affected, eight sustained 80 to 90 per cent damage, two were damaged by 30 to 40 per cent, while another sustained about 10 per cent damage,” he told a press conference at the scene here yesterday.
Mohd Suhaimi said four people, including a Singaporean, suffered breathing difficulties in the incident. However, only one was taken to Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) for further treatment and was reported to be in stable condition.

Title: Ramanan: Malaysians abroad encouraged to return, contribute skills and expertise
Article:
JAKARTA, Oct 7 — The government always welcomes Malaysians living abroad who wish to return home and bring their experience and expertise to the country, with various initiatives in place to facilitate their return.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the initiatives include the
Returning Expert Programme (REP)
, managed by Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp), as well as the MYFutureJobs portal under the Social Security Organisation (Perks), which offers more than 400,000 job opportunities.
“For me, the principle is simple, and this is something I always remind every KESUMA (Human Resources Ministry) officer. If we want Malaysian talent to return, we must make it easier, not make it more difficult. We are here to facilitate, not to complicate matters.
“Because we cannot tell them, ‘Come back to Malaysia’, but when they want to return, the process is so complicated that eventually they say, ‘Never mind. I’ll just stay in Jakarta.’ That is what we do not want,” he said in his speech at the Salam Dari Malaysia @ Jakarta programme here on Monday tonight.
Also present were Chargé d’Affaires ad interim of the Embassy of Malaysia in Jakarta Datuk Muzaffar Shah Mustafa, TalentCorp Group Chief Executive Officer Biruntha Mooruthi and Social Security Organisation (Perks) Group Chief Executive Officer Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed.
At the programme, Ramanan also launched the Guidelines for Applying for an Entry Permit under the REP category, in collaboration with the Malaysian Immigration Department. The guidelines provide clearer and more structured references, with the estimated processing period now shortened from about six months to around four months or less.
“The decision to return is not as simple as buying a plane ticket. There are careers to consider. Sometimes there are spouses, whether a wife, husband, girlfriend or boyfriend.
“Some have children who are in school, commitments and a family’s future to consider. That is why, when the government talks about bringing Malaysian talent home, we cannot look only at the individual. We also need to consider their families,” he said.
Introduced in 2001 and placed under TalentCorp’s management in 2011 to facilitate the return of Malaysian professionals living abroad, REP applications can be accessed through the
MyHeart.my
online platform.
Ramanan also stressed that opportunities to contribute to Malaysia need not wait until they return home.
“If you have expertise, please share it with Malaysia. If you have connections in Indonesia, or if you see opportunities for Malaysian companies or talent in Indonesia, please help us open those doors.
“Even if you are abroad, the experience you have gained here can still benefit Malaysians,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Dewan Rakyat to focus on sick projects, P. Ramlee copyright issues today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Strengthening contractor selection and performance assessment criteria to address delays in government projects and ‘sick projects’ is among the key issues to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper on the official Parliament website, Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (PN-Langkawi) will ask the Works Minister about proactive measures to address weaknesses in contractors’ management and financial capabilities, as well as new mechanisms to be introduced.
The latest developments on the proposed Parental Care Bill will also be raised by Rodiyah Sapiee (GPS-Batang Sadong), who will ask the Women, Family and Community Development Minister about the status of the bill.
She will also seek clarification on the form and mechanism of comprehensive social protection expected to be announced to safeguard the welfare of senior citizens amid the country’s demographic shift towards an ageing population.
Meanwhile, Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson) will ask the Education Minister to elaborate on the ministry’s preparedness to accommodate the simultaneous increase in six- and seven-year-old children entering Year One for the 2027 school session.
The preservation of artistic heritage will also be raised by Onn Abu Bakar (PH-Batu Pahat), who will ask the Communications Minister to provide an update on government initiatives to acquire or repurchase ownership and copyright rights, as well as management rights, to films by the late Tan Sri P. Ramlee for preservation as national heritage assets.
Following the oral question-and-answer session, the sitting will continue with the tabling of a motion by the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department on the Auditor-General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026, which was tabled last Monday.
The motion, among other things, calls on all relevant ministries, departments and agencies to examine the findings and recommendations of the audit report objectively to strengthen governance integrity and the management of public funds.
The sitting is also scheduled to continue with the second reading of the Food (Amendment) Bill 2026 by the Health Minister.
The Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, which began last Monday, is scheduled to run for 37 days until December 8. — Bernama

Title: FT minister announces gazettement of 88 more open-space lots
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — A total of 88 open-space lots in the Federal capital have been gazetted in the first nine months of this year, bringing the number of legally protected lots to 582, covering 476.17 hectares.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the latest gazettement involved 26 lots covering 7.33 hectares, equivalent to about 10 football fields.
“The gazettement provides clearer legal protection for open spaces and helps ensure they are preserved for public benefit.
“Open spaces also play an important role in the urban environment by helping to absorb rainwater runoff, reduce the effects of urban heat and provide recreational areas for the community,” she said in a Facebook post today.
Hannah said the latest 26 lots were located across eight parliamentary constituencies: Bandar Tun Razak (six lots), Segambut (five), Seputeh and Cheras (four each), Wangsa Maju, Lembah Pantai and Batu (two each), and Setiawangsa (one).
In Bandar Tun Razak, the areas are Alam Damai, Taman Damai Jaya and Taman Connaught, while in Segambut, they include Taman Segambut Indah, Taman Tun Dr Ismail, Taman Sri Hartamas, Taman Sri Kuching and Taman Sri Bintang.
In Seputeh, the lots are in Taman LTAT, Taman Shanghai, Bandar Bukit Jalil and Taman Esplanad, while Cheras involves Taman Midah, Taman Connaught and Taman Bukit Ria.
The other areas are Taman Desa Melawati and Taman Setapak (Wangsa Maju); Bukit Persekutuan/Jalan Travers (Lembah Pantai); Taman Kok Lian (Batu); and Taman Keramat AU3 (Setiawangsa).
The public can check the list, gazettement status and locations of all 582 open spaces via the MyHijau link on the official Federal Territories Land and Mines Office (PPTGWP) website at
www.ptgwp.gov.my
.
The facility allows Kuala Lumpur residents and residents’ associations to check the status of open spaces in their neighbourhoods and help monitor and preserve them. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Bahrain GP at SIC elevates Malaysia’s international image
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The successful hosting of the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Petronas Sepang International Circuit (SIC) last Sunday has elevated Malaysia’s international image.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said hosting the prestigious motorsport event allowed local fans to experience the thrill of F1 action on home soil again, while opening vast economic opportunities for local entrepreneurs.
“Special appreciation to Bahrain for the friendship that made this meaningful moment possible. May the close ties between our two nations continue to bloom,” he said in a post accompanying a highlight video of the F1 event on his Facebook page yesterday.
In the video, several local fans expressed gratitude for the chance to watch the world-class race, especially with ticket prices starting as low as RM200.
The Prime Minister also thanked all parties involved in making the race a success, creating special memories for Malaysians and F1 fans worldwide.
In July, F1 confirmed Malaysia as the host for the Gulf Air Bahrain GP from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement between Formula 1, the International Automobile Federation (FIA), and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain. It marked the event’s return to SIC after nine years.
The historic hosting followed discussions and the close friendship between His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia and the King of Bahrain, King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. The two governments then cooperated to ensure the race remained on the 2026 F1 calendar after it was cancelled earlier due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: MyGov Malaysia consolidates government services into one app
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Accessing key government services is now easier with the integration of driving licences, road tax, Road Transport Department (JPJ) summons checks, passports, government clinic appointments and Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) under a single platform: the MyGOV Malaysia app.
“No more hunting for government services in different places. We have brought various government services together into one app so that the public’s affairs are made simpler and smoother,” said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil in a video post on social media yesterday.
Fahmi added that the app also allows users to check unclaimed money, while other services will be integrated in phases.
Interestingly, Fahmi said MyGOV Malaysia also comes equipped with an ‘AI Chat’ feature, which allows users to obtain information and answers on government services directly.
“Our objective is simple. We are bringing all government services directly to the people in one complete app,” he emphasised.
He encouraged the public to take advantage of the digital facility by downloading MyGOV Malaysia for more convenient government services. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar: Adopt AI, but remain rooted in faith and heritage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Muslims must embrace new technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), to avoid being left behind in the rapid pace of global development, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the real challenge today was to harness technological advances such as quantum computing, AI and rapid digitalisation while remaining firmly rooted in the strength of faith, morals and personal character.
“People who failed to embrace AI as a new field of knowledge risked falling behind, but our understanding of AI does not necessarily mean copying or wholly adopting what comes from foreign countries, especially Western countries.
“We must preserve our values. In our pursuit of change and desire to acquire knowledge in artificial intelligence and other fields, we must remain grounded in the strength of what is known as our ‘turath’, our legacy and our heritage,” he said.
He said this when officiating the 66th International Quran Recital and Memorisation Assembly (MTHQA) at the World Trade Centre (WTC) here last night.
Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
Meanwhile, Anwar said any economic growth and modernisation agenda, including digital transformation, could not be pursued without peace and consensus among people of different races and religions.
Referring to relations among people as guided by the Quran, he said the holy book called on Muslims to know and respect one another’s differences to foster genuine harmony.
“That is why, in pursuing change, we must not lose sight of the spirit of bringing goodness and mercy. Dakwah must be driven by compassion, not by a desire to boast about our knowledge and intelligence.
“Peace comes from the consensus achieved among Muslims and non-Muslims in our country. No country in the world can pursue economic growth and development without the spirit of unity and peace,” he said.
The 66th MTHQA, held from October 6 to 10, carries the theme ‘Madani Dihayati, Ummah Diberkati’ and brings together 50 participants from 38 countries, comprising 25 participants in Quran recitation and 25 in Quran memorisation.
Malaysia is represented by Mohamad Cik Hasnul Taqiyuddin Cik Sazali and Nur Syakura Mohamad Musa in the Quran recitation category, and Muhammad Izzul Afnan Sazali and Dina Hadfina Mohd Umarul Hisyam in the Quran memorisation category. — Bernama

Title: Budget-tight Suhakam wants stronger public funding even if allowed to generate own revenue, says chairman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) has been operating on a shoestring budget for years despite taking on more responsibilities, its chairman Datuk Seri Mohd Hishamudin Md Yunus said.
Mohd Hishamudin said the funding gap has hampered Suhakam’s plans to widen its presence outside the Klang Valley and has limited its ability to launch probes and public engagements.
“Financial constraints require Suhakam to prioritise how its limited resources are used.
“The issue has become pressing as Suhakam’s statutory responsibilities have expanded,” he told Malay Mail during an exclusive interview recently.
Section 19(1) of the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia Act 1999 mandates the federal government to provide Suhakam with adequate funds annually for its operations.
The same Act also prohibits Suhakam from receiving foreign funds but Section 19(3) permits it to receive unconditional funds from individuals or organisations — strictly only to promote human rights awareness and education.
The Act also does not provide for Suhakam to generate its own revenue — an option that may ease the national human rights body’s ongoing cash flow woes.
Challenges from financial constraints
Mohd Hishamudin said nearly 90 per cent of Suhakam’s annual budget goes towards emoluments and essential operational expenditure, leaving only 10 per cent for programmes and activities.
The lean budget limits Suhakam’s capacity to conduct investigations, monitoring, human rights education, research, advocacy and public engagement.
Amendments to the Suhakam Act in 2024 and a slew of new laws passed since then have also left greater responsibilities on Suhakam’s shoulders.
Suhakam chairman Datuk Seri Mohd Hishamudin Md Yunus at Suhakam headquarters in Kuala Lumpur recently, where he spoke about the commission’s limited funding and expanding responsibilities. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
These include the formal institutionalisation of the Office of the Children’s Commissioner as well as its monitoring and advisory roles under the Online Safety Act 2025 and the Anti-Bullying Act 2026.
Plans to make the organisation more accessible to other parts of the country have also hit a snag.
Mohd Hishamudin said Suhakam could not establish proposed offices in the northern and east coast regions of the peninsula because of budget constraints.
Some of Suhakam’s approved financial commitments were also delivered almost a year late because of budget constraints. For instance, the revised remuneration for Suhakam commissioners, which was approved in November 2025, only took effect in September 2026 after Suhakam received the necessary funds.
Own revenue cannot replace government funding
On July 1, Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran told the Dewan Rakyat that the government is reviewing suggestions to allow Suhakam to generate its own revenue through training and related programmes.
Mohd Hishamudin welcomed the plan but stressed an important caveat: Public funding must remain the foundation of Suhakam’s funding.
“Any income Suhakam is permitted to generate should supplement, not substitute, government funding,” Mohd Hishamudin said.
Mohd Hishamudin also said that Suhakam’s reliance on government funding does not affect its independence since institutions like Parliament, the courts and even several oversight bodies are publicly funded.
However, he pointed out that stronger statutory safeguards concerning funding and the appointments and tenure of Suhakam commissioners would reinforce public confidence in that independence.
“As such, Suhakam respectfully appeals to the Government to provide it with adequate funding.
“We are not asking for more. We are only asking for what we are entitled to under the Suhakam Act and the Paris Principles: adequate funding.”

Title: Nearly 51 years later, daughter of former Perak police chief Khoo Chong Kong remembers the man behind his uniform
Article:
TANJONG MALIM, Oct 6 — Time may have passed, but the image of the late former Perak police chief Tan Sri Khoo Chong Kong as a loving father and a firm, courageous police officer remains vivid for his daughter, Datin Rita Koo Swee Kim.
Rita, 78, said a pantomime performance held in conjunction with the official opening of the Muallim District Police Headquarters (IPD) today rekindled memories of her father, nearly 51 years after his death, leaving her deeply moved.
“I was 25 at the time and living in Seremban (Negeri Sembilan) after getting married. I received a call from a police officer telling me that something had happened to my father, but I was given no further details.
“When we heard the news, my husband and I rushed back to Ipoh to see my father and find out what had happened to him. He had been attacked with a weapon. I’m really touched that the Royal Malaysia Police, especially the Perak police, still remember him after all these years,” she said when met here today.
Datin Rita Koo Swee Kim (second left), daughter of the late former Perak police chief Tan Sri Koo Chong Kong, poses with her husband and child beside the original uniform worn by Koo when he was shot dead by communist elements on November 13, 1975, at an exhibition in Ipoh on October 6, 2026. — Bernama pic
Earlier, the Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah officiated the opening of the Muallim IPD.
Rita, Khoo’s eldest daughter, said one of the memories closest to her heart was how devoted her father was to his work, often spending long hours on duty, particularly during his service with the Special Branch and operations to combat communist activities.
She said there were times when her father had to be away from home for one or two months to carry out operations, leaving her mother worried about his safety.
“He was always very busy. There were times when he would leave for an operation and be gone for one or two months. We never knew exactly when he would be coming home,” she said.
Rita said that despite his firm and serious demeanour while on duty, her father was a loving and caring man at home.
Datin Rita Koo Swee Kim, daughter of the late former Perak police chief Tan Sri Koo Chong Kong, speaks during an interview at an exhibition held in conjunction with the opening of the Muallim District Police Headquarters in Ipoh on October 6, 2026. — Bernama pic
She also described him as a man who stood firmly by his principles and would not compromise on what he believed was right, saying his courage in carrying out his duties had always been an inspiration to her.
Meanwhile, Rita said seeing the official car her father once used and the blood-stained uniform he wore during the incident was an emotional experience, bringing back memories of her father and the sacrifice he made in the line of duty.
“It really takes me back to those days. I had seen the car at a museum before, but seeing it again today, together with his uniform and hearing the stories about him, really brought back so many memories,” she said.
Born on November 12, 1925, in Kwangsi, China, the late Khoo was raised in Ipoh and joined the Sarawak Constabulary as an inspector on November 5, 1952, before holding several key positions and eventually becoming Perak police chief on January 7, 1975.
Beside the official car once used by her late father, former Perak police chief Tan Sri Koo Chong Kong, Datin Rita Koo Swee Kim (right) poses with her child at an exhibition in Ipoh on October 6, 2026. Koo was shot dead by communist elements on November 13, 1975. — Bernama pic
He was shot while travelling home from the Perak Police Contingent Headquarters to his residence on Jalan Tawar, Ipoh, at about 1pm on November 13, 1975, in an attack believed to have been carried out by communist insurgents.
His driver, Corporal Yeong Peng Cheong, was also killed in the attack, while Khoo succumbed to his injuries on November 14, 1975, about 28 hours after he was shot. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: IPD is the abbreviation in Malay for Ibu Pejabat Polis Daerah (District Police Headquarters).

Title: ‘A happy family?’: Zara Qairina’s stepsister says she never met teen, but regularly viewed photos on social media
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 6 — The stepsister of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir told the Coroner’s Court that she never lived with the teenager and had no first-hand knowledge of how Zara Qairina’s mother cared for and raised her.
Malianah Mahathir, 25, the 81st witness, said she only knew of Zara Qairina’s life and family from social media posts as well as information from her father.
When questioned by lawyer Shahlan Jufri, who represents Zara Qairina’s mother, Malianah said she had seen photographs of the family through the Facebook accounts of Zara Qairina, her mother and her father.
“I only saw them through Facebook posts. I used to stalk their photos all the time. A happy family, right?” she said before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan during today’s inquest proceedings.
She said her father often uploaded family photographs, including ones of Zara Qairina as a baby and pictures of holidays they took together.
When answering questions from Coroner Amir Shah, Malianah confirmed that she had never met or interacted personally with Zara Qairina at any point between the teenager’s birth and her death.
She also acknowledged that all the information she knew about Zara Qairina was obtained from what others had told her, and not from the teenager herself.
Malianah further agreed that her testimony in court concerning unpleasant experiences she had endured was related to Zara Qairina’s mother, and not to experiences with Zara Qairina herself.
The Coroner then asked whether Zara Qairina’s mother had treated her badly every day throughout the period they lived together, to which Malianah replied: “Ah, no.”
When questioned by lawyer Nurul Rafeeqa Afdul Mutolip, who represents Zara Qairina’s father, Malianah also admitted that when she first moved in with Zara Qairina’s mother, she was initially happy to have a “new mum” and had been treated well.
Zara Qairina died at Queen Elizabeth Hospital on July 17, 2025, a day after the Form One student was found unconscious near a drain at her school hostel at 4am.
The inquest proceedings resume tomorrow with new witnesses. — Bernama

Title: Myanmar president to visit Malaysia tomorrow as migrant returns draw rights groups’ warnings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Myanmar’s coup leader turned president Min Aung Hlaing will head to Malaysia on Wednesday for a two-day visit, officials said, following Kuala Lumpur’s plan to return thousands of Myanmar immigrants.
The visit comes after a group of nearly 1,500 returnees reached Myanmar on Sunday, with rights groups warning Rohingya refugees could be among those sent back.
Malaysia said about 5,000 Myanmar nationals have agreed to “voluntary” return, but authorities have not commented on the ethnicities of those who have returned.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim “will hold talks with President Min Aung Hlaing on key bilateral issues, including the voluntary, dignified and safe repatriation of Myanmar nationals of all ethnic groups who have been in Malaysia illegally,” Malaysia’s Foreign Affairs Ministry said on Tuesday.
“The Leaders are also expected to review the ongoing efforts undertaken under the Asean mechanisms” for peace in Myanmar, the ministry said in a statement.
Earlier on Tuesday, Anwar told the Malaysian parliament he and other top Malaysian officials “will raise issues towards a solution”.
Growing hostility
Naypyidaw has repatriated nearly 10,000 migrants from Malaysia this year, its state media said on Monday.
Anwar said Myanmar had to “guarantee proper treatment to their own people so that there is no abuse, oppression and violation of human rights”.
“But for me, any country that wants to bring back their people from our country, we welcome that,” Anwar said.
The Malaysian visit will be among Min Aung Hlaing’s most diplomatically significant since Asean leaders froze out Myanmar’s junta following the 2021 coup and ensuing civil war.
But Anwar said last month he would welcome the Myanmar leader to expedite migrant repatriations.
“I want to tell him that we can be friends and trade.
“We can accept Myanmar, but they must accept (their refugees) back,” Anwar said during a podcast interview.
The repatriation plan follows what Malaysia’s human rights commission has called “growing hostility, discriminatory rhetoric and online attacks” against the Rohingya in Muslim-majority Malaysia.
Malaysia hosts more than 215,000 refugees and asylum seekers registered with the United Nations refugee agency, including more than 126,000 Rohingya from Myanmar — its largest refugee community.
The UN and rights groups have raised concerns about the repatriations, with monitors fearing the Rohingya could face a new wave of abuses in Myanmar, where they are denied full citizenship.
Rights advocates view Min Aung Hlaing as the primary architect of a crackdown against the group, starting in 2017, which is being weighed by the International Court of Justice as potential genocide.
‘No time to return’
Myanmar this month pledged “safe and dignified” returns for its citizens displaced abroad.
Myanmar is also riven by violence, with 50 killed last week in a military airstrike on a marketplace in western Rakhine state.
“This is no time to return anyone forcibly to a country plagued by egregious human rights violations and abuses,” UN rights chief Volker Turk said last week.
Min Aung Hlaing ousted the elected government of Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi in February 2021, plunging Myanmar into a civil war that has killed more than 100,000 people, according to monitor ACLED.
Since elections that were widely dismissed as a charade, Min Aung Hlaing became civilian leader and launched a drive for regional recognition.
Asean has frozen Myanmar’s top leaders out of its summits since the coup over a lack of engagement with its roadmap to end the civil war.
After 2021, the bloc presented a united front, demanding Myanmar engage with its five-point plan to bring peace through dialogue between all sides.
But analysts have warned the consensus is now fracturing, with some Asean nations now welcoming Min Aung Hlaing.
Malaysia will be the fifth nation of the 11-member Asean bloc – following Thailand, Laos, Vietnam and Cambodia – to welcome him since taking up the presidency.
He has also visited China – which previously backed him behind the scenes, according to analysts – as well as India and Russia. — AFP

Title: Fishmonger fined RM5,000 for peeping at neighbour in shower
Article:
KUALA KRAI, Oct 6 — The Magistrate’s Court here today fined a fishmonger RM5,000 after he pleaded guilty to peeping at his neighbour’s wife last month.
Magistrate Rais Imran Hamid also ordered Tuan Ahmad Farid Tuan Mat, 36, to serve nine months in prison if he fails to pay the fine.
The man was charged with peeping at the 26-year-old victim while she was taking a bath at a house in Jalan Halimah Guchil here at about 11.30am on September 28, with the intention or knowledge that it would cause fear, anxiety or distress to the victim regarding her safety.
The charge was framed under Section 507A (1) of the Penal Code, punishable under the same section, which carries a maximum prison term of three years or a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Earlier, Deputy Public Prosecutor Mazlinda Mohd Nor urged the court to impose a deterrent sentence in the public interest and to serve as a lesson to prevent the accused from repeating the offence.
However, counsel Farazalila Fauzi from the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK), representing Tuan Ahmad Farid, pleaded for a minimum fine on the grounds that her client is single, earns about RM50 daily as a fishmonger, and supports his 66-year-old mother who has cancer.

Title: Ahead of Budget 2027, World Bank tells Putrajaya to raise revenue without raising rates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Malaysia needs tax reform to address a structural decline in its tax revenue-to-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio, which has fallen to 12.7 per cent from 15 per cent 15 years ago, according to the World Bank lead economist Apurva Sanghi.
He said the federal government debt has risen to over 65 per cent of GDP although the fiscal deficit has been contained, however, this would not be enough to bring the debt-to-GDP ratio down to the target of 60 per cent by 2028.
“Federal government debt rose despite the contained deficit and now stands at 65.2 per cent.
“The cost of servicing debt is also increasing, with 17 sen of every ringgit in revenue raised spent on debt servicing,” he told the media during a briefing on October 2026 East Asia and Pacific Economic Update here today.
Yesterday, the Auditor General’s Report 2/2026 reported that federal government debt stood at RM1.32 trillion in 2025 compared with RM1.24 trillion in 2024, while the statutory debt stood at RM1.295 trillion, comprising Malaysian Government Securities, Malaysian Government Investment Issues and Malaysian Islamic Treasury Bills.
Apurva said that while increasing tax rates would be difficult, there were ways to raise tax revenue without doing so.
Responding to a question on taxation and Budget 2027, which will be tabled this Friday, he said simplifying the corporate tax system for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) by consolidating the tax structure would benefit businesses.
“Apart from that, when an SME grows and becomes a non-SME, its favourable tax rate is suddenly taken away. We call this a tax curve, and it reduces the incentive for SMEs to officially grow bigger. As we know, about 98 per cent of Malaysian companies are SMEs. Changing the incentive structure to encourage firms to graduate from SME status can help,” he added.
He also said that it would be good to see the budget make the tax system more supportive of investment.
“To be precise, consider allowing qualifying investments to fully cover 100 per cent of the investment cost,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Socso cuts benefit claim processing time to 2.7 days from 5.3 days
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) has reduced the processing time for contributor benefit claims from an average of 5.3 days in 2024 to 2.7 days as of last year.
Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan said the service delivery improvement was carried out in compliance with the Client Charter to ensure quality standards remain at an optimal level.
He said the initial response time for complaint processing was also shortened from three days in 2024 to just one day in 2025.
“Beginning 2025, the processing time for each benefit application under the Employment Injury Scheme, Self-Employment Social Security Scheme and Housewives’ Social Security Scheme has been reduced from an average of 5.3 days the previous year to 2.7 days in 2025,” he said.
He was responding to a question from V. Ganabatirau (PH-Klang), who asked about reforms to improve Perkeso’s operational efficiency as well as the mismatch between the Invalidity Pension rate and the current cost of living.
He said that from January 1 to December 31, 2025, Perkeso’s Client Charter performance for the overall benefit claim and payment process across the three schemes averaged 96.86 per cent.
Addressing the issue of the Invalidity Pension, Khairul Firdaus said the government does not set pension rates arbitrarily, but rather reviews them periodically every three to five years.
He said these reviews take into account the rising cost of living, inflation rates and the sustainability of the organisation’s funds.
“Indicators and mechanisms for determining increases in the minimum pension rate, implemented by the ministry and Perkeso, are based on actuarial assessment studies by the International Labour Organisation, taking into consideration the current social and economic conditions in our country,” he said.
He added that the findings serve as a key benchmark in ensuring monthly payments are sufficient to help recipients make ends meet. — Bernama
Note: Perkeso is also known as Socso, the English acronym for Social Security Organisation.

Title: Chest a minute! Diner allegedly plucks out body hair and plants it in ‘char kway teow’ to dodge RM30 bill in Penang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — A diner in Penang allegedly plucked hair from his own chest and planted it in a plate of
char kway teow
before claiming the food was contaminated and refusing to pay the RM30 bill.
The alleged ruse was only discovered after the restaurant manager checked CCTV footage, which he said appeared to show the man repeatedly reaching inside his clothes before placing something into the dish.
The incident is believed to have happened at a restaurant along Persiaran Gurney in George Town at about 5pm on Sunday, October 4, according to
Sin Chew Daily
, as reported by
The Star
.
The restaurant manager, identified only as Cheng, said the man, believed to be a foreign national, and his companion had initially wanted to order fried chicken but chose
char kway teow
, an egg and a drink after being told the chicken was sold out.
Cheng said the man later complained that he had found hair in the noodles.
“After examining it, I found that something was amiss,” he was quoted as saying.
“If the hair had really been in the
char kway teow
, it should have been oily, but the hair we found was dry.
“There were six to seven strands of hair in the dish. They were also very short and did not look like eyelashes.”
Cheng said the couple then got up to leave while restaurant staff were still examining the food.
When reminded that they had not paid, the man allegedly refused, saying he would not pay for food that had been contaminated.
Suspicious, Cheng later reviewed the restaurant’s CCTV footage.
He claimed the recording appeared to show the man repeatedly putting his hand inside his clothes, pulling out what looked like chest hair and placing it into the
char kway teow
.
The meal cost about RM30.
Cheng said the CCTV footage had since been shared with other restaurant operators to warn them about the couple.

Title: KLIA incident involving border agency chief: AGC to examine witness statements, evidence before deciding on further action
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) will examine witness statements, closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage and various other evidence before deciding on further action in connection with an incident involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said this after the AGC confirmed receiving the investigation papers on the case, which occurred at Terminal 1 of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on September 28.
He said all evidence gathered during the investigation would be thoroughly examined to enable the AGC to determine the next course of action.
“The AGC will examine every aspect of the investigation before any further action can be taken in connection with this case,” he said when contacted today.
Yesterday, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the investigation papers had been submitted to the AGC for review, advice and further directions in accordance with Article 145(3) of the Federal Constitution.
So far, 25 witnesses have had their statements recorded to assist in the investigation.
The investigation is being conducted by the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which covers the offence of voluntarily causing hurt, illness or bodily weakness to another person.
Mohd Shuhaily had previously said that he left it to the government to decide on any action that might be taken against him following a viral video showing him reprimanding two individuals at KLIA Terminal 1. — Bernama

Title: Johor Regent receives MACC chief, new state director at Istana Pasir Pelangi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Regent of Johor Tunku Mahkota Ismail granted an audience to Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman at Istana Pasir Pelangi yesterday.
According to a statement posted on His Royal Highness’ official Facebook page, the new Johor MACC director Datuk Hazrul Shazreen Abd Yazid, whose appointment took effect on October 1, was also present during the audience.
“During the meeting, the MACC leadership conveyed the agency’s continued commitment to strengthening anti-corruption enforcement and prevention, as well as integrity and governance in the state.
“The meeting reflects the continuing working relationship between the MACC and the Johor Royal Institution in supporting the agenda of integrity and good governance,” the statement said. — Bernama

Title: E-hailing driver tests positive for meth after crash kills 22-year-old Maldivian student near PJS toll
Article:
SUBANG JAYA, Oct 6 — An e-hailing driver tested positive for methamphetamine in a urine screening test after a crash on the New Pantai Expressway (NPE) that killed a 22-year-old female student from the Maldives,
Harian Metro
reported.
The 37-year-old driver was carrying two Maldivian women when his Perodua Ativa collided with a Proton S70 near the PJS Toll Plaza at about 8.48pm on Sunday, according to Subang Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat.
Police said the Ativa spun and overturned in the middle of the road following the impact.
“One of the passengers was trapped in the vehicle and pronounced dead at the scene, while the other was injured,” Wan Azlan was quoted as saying.
Both women, aged 22, were students at a private higher education institution in the Klang Valley.
According to police investigations, the Proton S70, driven by a 34-year-old local man, was heading towards the RFID lane when the rear right side of the car was struck by the Ativa from the right.
Wan Azlan said urine screening tests were carried out on both drivers following the crash.
The e-hailing driver tested positive for methamphetamine, also known locally as syabu, he said.
A Shah Alam Magistrates’ Court subsequently granted police a four-day remand order against the driver to assist investigations.
“The case is being investigated under Section 44(1)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987, and the investigation papers are expected to be submitted to the Deputy Public Prosecutor tomorrow for further instructions,” Wan Azlan said.
The body of the victim was taken to the Serdang Hospital Forensic Department for a post-mortem examination.
Police have urged witnesses or motorists with dashcam footage of the crash to contact investigating officer Inspector Azizul Hakim Roslan at 011-2891 4495 or the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division at the Subang Jaya district police headquarters.

Title: Three crocodiles, including 4.75m giant, captured in Sarawak’s Batang Igan
Article:
SIBU, Oct 6 — Three large-sized crocodiles measuring between 2.44 metres and 4.75 metres were captured within the last three days in Sungai Batang Igan near Ulu Kampung Kebuaw, Igan, near here.
Licensed crocodile hunter Jeferry Siew Seng Kwong said the largest of the three, measuring 4.75 metres and estimated to weigh 500 kilogrammes, was captured at about 2.30am today by his four-member team with the assistance of villagers.
“The residents sought our help following frequent sightings of crocodiles in the area, including an incident in which one attacked a pet dog, causing concern among the villagers.
“After the crocodile was captured, the residents also helped us lift it onto the boat,” he told Bernama today.
Jeferry said the operation in the area began on October 3, with three crocodiles captured so far.
Two crocodiles measuring about 2.44 metres and 2.74 metres respectively were captured on October 4 and 5, before the largest, measuring 4.75 metres, was captured.
He said his team also found a nest containing about 40 crocodile eggs while conducting the operation.
Jeferry expressed his appreciation to the residents of Kampung Kebuaw for their cooperation and teamwork throughout the operation, as well as to Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) for its cooperation.
He said since obtaining a licence to hunt the reptile two years ago, he had captured over 100 crocodiles. — Bernama
